Job Title:Associate Professor or Professor, Director of the Arts and Humanities Artificial Intelligence Institute
Department:Arts and Sciences | Office of the Deans
James Mitchell Endowed Chair and Arts & Humanities Artificial Intelligence Institute Center Director Rank: Advanced Associate Professor or ProfessorCollege of Arts and SciencesPosition OverviewThe Ohio State University seeks the James Mitchell Endowed Chair who will be a center director to provide ambitious and innovative leadership for its newly established Arts and Humanities Artificial Intelligence Institute (AHAII). The aim is to make Ohio State a national hub in the conversation about what it means to be human in the age of AI. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027. The director will serve as the administrative head of an emerging and thriving institute, with oversight of facilities, budget, and strategic direction. In addition to their role as the institute leader and administrator, the director will also be a dedicated teacher and distinguished scholar, with a record of accomplishment to merit a tenure-track appointment in an Arts or Humanities department as an advanced Associate Professor or Professor.
The new director is expected to foster a collegial and interdisciplinary culture among a community of faculty, staff, and students from varied disciplinary backgrounds. They will be an advocate for the institute and its affiliated faculty and students, providing support and mentorship for scholarly activity while amplifying the voice of the arts and humanities in conversations around AI. Applying their knowledge in developing approaches, manifestations, and discourse tied to matters of AI, the director will guide institute affiliates, outreach endeavors, and student education. The director will have the opportunity to shape renovation plans for AHAII in Hughes Hall, a historic building on the oval and future home of our English Department. The director should be poised to engage with students, faculty, staff, and alumni to build collaborations with arts and humanities departments and interdisciplinary initiatives across the College of Arts and Sciences and the broader university community, Ohio State’s five regional campuses, and community organizations in Ohio and beyond.The successful candidate will be a dedicated educator and a recognized scholar and/or practitioner with expertise in one or more scholarly areas involving artificial intelligence and arts or humanities and will have a 50% FTE (Full Time Equivalent) faculty appointment in an appointment in one of the 21 Arts and Humanities departments in the College of Arts and Sciences with the other 50% FTE appointment as AHAII director.Performance Objectives
To provide steady yet innovative leadership to AHAII.
To support fundraising efforts in partnership with OSU Advancement.
Initiating and partnering on writing grants and exploring industry connections to support AHAII.
To manage budgets, resources, and space for the institute.
To coordinate arts, humanities, and artificial intelligence initiatives in teaching, scholarship, and engagement in and beyond the college.
To help faculty, students, and staff thrive in their roles through leadership, mentoring, and professional development.
To advocate for the institute to units around the university, community, and broader academic field.
To lead engagement efforts with communities and public/private organizations in and beyond Central Ohio.
Education and Experience RequirementsRequired:
Applicants are expected to have an appropriate terminal degree in an area of specialty sufficient to warrant appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor with tenure.
National/international record of scholarly or artistic achievement in AI, arts and/or humanities commensurate with the position of advanced Associate Professor or Professor at the Ohio State University, including a distinguished record of creative or scholarly achievement, teaching excellence at the post-secondary level, and professional service; and evidence of continued excellence in creative and/or scholarly achievement. Equivalent outstanding achievement in industry will also be considered.
Demonstrated and effective leadership and administrative experience in academia.
Demonstrated ability to cultivate positive work relationships with students, colleagues, and staff.
Experience in leading and the ability to work successfully across disciplines within a diverse and complex organization.
Experience with interdisciplinary collaborations, for example those with other academic units, community partners, and professional academic/arts and humanities organizations.
Desired:
Experience in fundraising, budgeting, and management.
Experience managing an academic program, department, or center.
Additional Information
Ohio State provides access to a depth and breadth of opportunities and resources. Starting your first day, Ohio State offers you a comprehensive benefits package.
How to Apply
To be considered, please submit your application electronically via Workday https://osu.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/OSUCareers/job/Columbus-Campus/Associate-Professor-or-Professor--Director-of-the-Arts-and-Humanities-Artificial-Intelligence-Institute_R159362-1 .
Application deadline closes on November 1, 2026.
Application materials consist of the following required elements: a cover letter, curriculum vitae, and separate research and teaching statements. Inquiries may be directed to the Chair of the Search Committee, Professor Chris Coleman (coleman.1299@osu.edu).
You will be presented with the opportunity to attach up to THREE documents in the Application Documents section. Please include the following:
Attachment 1: Cover Letter: 3-4 page letter, which should include a summary of your leadership experience, overview of your teaching and research and/or creative scholarship, and your philosophy on AI with regards to the Arts and Humanities
Attachment 2: CV (Curriculum Vitae): Detailed overview of your scholarly experience, leadership experience, teaching and mentoring experience, service, funding, and publications.
Attachment 3: Research Statement: Summary of your past research/creative accomplishments, current work, and proposal for your future research plan as a faculty member.
You may be asked for names and contact information for three reference letters at a later date.
Additional Information:
The College
With more than 80 majors and 100 minors, the College of Arts and Sciences is the academic heart of the university. The Arts and Sciences provides extraordinary opportunities to collaborate across disciplines, blending creativity and analysis to truly be at the forefront of thought. The breadth and depth of knowledge in the college gives students and researchers the critical thinking and adaptability essential for a lifetime of success.
Center Information
AHAII was created in 2025 to coordinate, accelerate, and extend the reach of research, creative work, and public engagement centered on artificial intelligence. This focused hub serves as a vital advocate for the centrality of humanity in every conversation about the shape and use of AI. It builds on more than three-years of activity from more than two dozen interdisciplinary faculty working groups that have explored innovative uses of AI in arts and humanities research; the changing meanings of authorship and creativity; and the ethical, ecological, and social consequences of AI technologies. That work has, among other things, resulted in three new credentials that can be pursued alongside any undergraduate major: certificates in “AI and the Arts” (forthcoming); in “AI, Language, and Mind”; and in “AI, Ethics, and Society.” AHAII will be housed in Hughes Hall as soon as it reopens. Hughes, dedicated in 1949, is the former home to the School of Music and the final significant project in our Arts District. When renovated, it will have a new glass annex facing the Oval, and be home to the Department of English as well as AHAII, linking together our arts and humanities departments.
The University
Ohio State is a top-20 public university, and its Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is one of America’s leading academic health centers. Eligible Ohio State employees receive comprehensive benefits packages, including medical, dental and vision insurance, tuition assistance for employees and their dependents, and state or alternative retirement options with competitive employer contributions.

The area offers a wide range of affordable housing, many cultural and recreational opportunities, excellent schools, and a strong economy based on government as well as service, transportation, and technology industries. Additional information about the Columbus area is available here. Beyond its Columbus campus, Ohio State has four regional campuses including Ohio State Lima, Ohio State Mansfield, Ohio State Marion, and Ohio State Newark, in addition to the College of Food, Agricultural, and Environmental Sciences (CFAES) Wooster Campus, which houses Ohio State ATI.

The Department of Political Science at The Ohio State University invites applications for a faculty position at the rank of assistant professor. Successful applicants will have research and teaching interests in any of the following areas: methodological developments at the intersection of social science and AI/machine learning; the social and political consequences of reliance on algorithmic approaches to public policy implementation; the regulatory, political, or ethical challenges of the burgeoning reliance on AI in the public and/or private sectors.
Based in Columbus, Ohio, the position will begin in the fall of 2027. Preferred applicants will demonstrate the potential for a sustained and substantial body of work focusing on one or more of these areas. The position is open with respect to substantive focus or disciplinary subfield in Political Science. This position is part of the investment of The Ohio State University Provost in the Department of Political Science in Socio-Political Analysis and AI: https://polisci.osu.edu/good-to-great-proposal. The successful candidate will join a broader departmental initiative on socio-political analysis and AI that includes recent hires working on political methodology and the development of AI tools for social science research. This initiative provides substantial opportunities for intellectual exchange and cross-unit grant collaboration across methodological and substantive areas.

College of Arts and Sciences
Position Overview
The School of Communication at The Ohio State University Columbus campus invites applications for a 9-month full-time professional-practice faculty position in journalism at the rank of Professional-Practice Assistant Professor, to begin August 2027. We seek an experienced journalism professional who is a committed, experienced educator to play a central role in the School’s undergraduate journalism program.
This position will strengthen instruction in core journalism courses, particularly in core courses such as COMM 2221: Media Writing & Editing, COMM 3405: Lantern TV, and/or COMM 3403: Sports Writing. We anticipate growing demand in these and related areas as our new Sports Communication certificate and Sport, Society and Communication minor continue to expand. Depending on the successful candidate's expertise, the position may also support more regular offerings of advanced journalism skills courses, such as COMM 4202: Feature Writing.
Experience with news writing, editing, data journalism, investigative reporting, podcasting, public records, visual journalism, media law or other areas of contemporary journalism would further expand the courses the faculty member could support. Experience in multimedia journalism and/or sports journalism is desirable but not required. A candidate who can move comfortably among writing, editing, sports reporting and digital production would provide the greatest flexibility for the program. We are especially interested in candidates who can bring current professional knowledge, practical newsroom experience, and a student-centered approach to teaching and mentoring.
The successful candidate will contribute to a journalism program recognized for integrating writing, reporting, editing and multimedia production, helping students develop the versatile skills needed to succeed across today’s media platforms.
Performance Objectives
Teach and mentor undergraduate students in journalism and related areas.
Provide high-quality instruction in foundational and advanced journalism skills courses.
Support experiential learning opportunities connected to student media and related production-based courses.
Contribute to curriculum development and student preparation for a changing media landscape.
Maintain current knowledge in journalism practice and bring that knowledge into the classroom.
Embody the highest ethical and professional standards of journalism.
Contribute service to the School, College, University, and/or profession as appropriate for a professional-practice faculty appointment.
Education and Experience Requirements
Required:
Candidates must have either a doctorate in communication, journalism, or a related field, or a master’s degree along with equivalent and substantial industry/professional experience in journalism. Candidates should demonstrate substantial professional expertise relevant to the area of appointment and the ability to teach multiple undergraduate journalism courses effectively.
Desired:
Evidence of teaching excellence is highly desirable. Preference will be given to candidates whose professional experience expands the School's teaching capacity in media writing and editing, multimedia and digital journalism, sports journalism, feature writing, student media, or other areas of applied journalism practice. Experience mentoring students, supervising student media production, or developing strong curriculum and experiential learning opportunities is also desirable.

Cover Letter: 1-2 page letter, which should include a brief summary of your academic background and why you are interested in this opportunity.
CV (Curriculum Vitae): Detailed overview of your scholarly experience, including your research experience, teaching and mentoring experience, service, funding, and publications.
Research Statement: Summary of your past research accomplishments, current work/research, and proposal for your future research plan as a faculty member.
Teaching Statement: A statement of your approaches, experience and philosophy regarding your teaching, learning, and mentoring.
A writing sample
Letters of Reference: Candidates selected to move forward in the process will be asked to provide three letters of reference.

Clinical assistant professor of audiology

College of Arts and Sciences
Position Overview
The Department of Speech and Hearing Science in the College of Arts and Sciences at The Ohio State University invites applications for a clinical-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Clinical Professor in Audiology.
This position includes providing high-quality, evidence-based audiologic care within The Ohio State University Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic; precepting and mentoring Doctor of Audiology (AuD) students in clinical practice; teaching within the AuD curriculum; and contributing to the service and scholarly missions of the department. The successful candidate will join a collaborative team committed to excellence in patient care, clinical education, student mentorship, community engagement, and professional leadership. We seek a colleague who is enthusiastic about contributing to a dynamic academic and clinical environment and is committed to the continued growth and success of our programs.
Performance Objectives
Teach, model, and provide high-quality, evidence-based audiologic (and related) care while serving a diverse patient population and providing clinical education within The Ohio State University Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic.
Teach graduate-level courses in audiology in alignment with departmental needs and the candidate's areas of expertise.
Support the daily operation and advancement of the clinic; this may include oversight of clinical resources, equipment, technologies, software systems, clinical spaces, and other operational activities necessary to support an efficient and patient-centered clinical environment.
Participate in program-related and professional service activities, including committee work, admissions, assessment initiatives, outreach activities, and departmental events.
Engage in research or scholarly activities, including the supervision and mentorship of student capstone projects.
Support the mission of the clinic, department, and university through collaboration, flexibility, versatility, and a shared commitment to student success, patient care, and program excellence.
Education and Experience Requirements
Required: Applicants must hold a Doctor of Audiology (AuD) degree or equivalent doctoral degree in audiology and be eligible for audiology licensure in the State of Ohio.
Applicants must have:
Experience in comprehensive audiologic assessment and hearing loss rehabilitation, including amplification.
A commitment to excellence in clinical education and interest in teaching in both clinical and classroom settings.
The ability to work collaboratively with faculty, staff, and students in a varied, dynamic work environment while supporting a culture of teamwork, adaptability, and shared responsibility.
Initiative, flexibility, and a commitment to collaborating with colleagues in support of shared program goals.
A commitment to evidence-based practice, professional growth, and the development of future audiologists.
Desired:
Interest and experience in developing or expanding clinical services, educational initiatives, or other activities that enhance the program’s impact in clinical education, within the profession, and community.
Additional expertise in specialized areas of audiology (e.g., vestibular assessment and management, tinnitus, electrophysiology, cochlear implants, or related areas) is welcomed, and applicants are encouraged to highlight those experiences.
Additional Information
Ohio State provides access to a depth and breadth of opportunities and resources. Starting your first day, Ohio State offers you a comprehensive benefits package.
How to Apply
To be considered, please submit your application electronically via Workday.
A complete application consists of the following required elements: cover letter, curriculum vitae, teaching statement, and three professional references.
To be considered, please submit the following:
Attachment 1: Cover Letter (1-2 pages): Describing your professional background, clinical expertise, interest in the position, and qualifications for the role. Applicants are encouraged to address experiences in clinical education, student mentorship, professional growth, program development, and working collaboratively within clinical and academic teams.
Attachment 2: Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Professional Resume: A curriculum vitae or professional resume detailing clinical experience, teaching and mentoring activities, professional service, presentations, certifications, and other relevant accomplishments.
Attachment 3: Professional Interests, Perspectives, and/or Teaching Statement (1-2 pages): Please provide a brief statement describing your professional, clinical, and/or teaching values, philosophies, and perspectives that you believe are most relevant to this position. This statement is intended to help the search committee understand what you would bring to the role beyond what is reflected in your CV, resume, or cover letter. Applicants are encouraged to focus on the areas that best represent their professional identity, values, and interests, and are not expected to address every topic listed below.
Topics may include:( Philosophy or approach to patient care, Philosophy or approach to clinical education, teaching, precepting, or mentorship, Perspectives on collaboration, teamwork, and contributing to a shared mission, Professional values and guiding principles, Leadership, service, or program development interests, Professional growth and future aspirations)
Attachment 4: Professional References: A list of the names, titles, and email addresses of three professional references. Letters of recommendation will be requested only for candidates selected to move forward in the process.
The application period will close on November 15, 2025, and review of applications will begin at that time. Inquiries may be directed to Jodi Baxter, AuD at baxter.216@osu.edu.

Job Title:Physician - Family and Community Health, Family Medicine Physician (Open Rank/Track Faculty)
Department:
The Department of Family and Community Medicine at The Ohio State University College of Medicine seeks a board-certified or board-eligible family medicine physician to join our faculty on the Clinician Scholar Pathway. This position is intended for physician-scholars who are committed to advancing family medicine through a combination of excellent clinical care, teaching, scholarship, and innovation. The successful candidate will maintain an active clinical practice while contributing substantially to the department's academic mission through research, quality improvement, implementation science, medical education scholarship, population health initiatives, health services research, or other scholarly activities aligned with primary care.
The successful candidate will develop and lead a focused program of scholarship with measurable impact in family medicine and primary care. Faculty are expected to contribute to peer-reviewed scholarship, collaborate across disciplines, mentor learners, pursue external funding opportunities, and disseminate scholarly work through publications, presentations, and other academic venues. Candidates should demonstrate the ability to integrate clinical practice with scholarship and build a recognized area of expertise that advances patient care, healthcare delivery, medical education, or population health.
Faculty will practice within a collaborative, team-based primary care environment that includes physicians, trainees, pharmacists, social workers, behavioral health specialists, and other interdisciplinary partners. Academic rank, clinical effort, and scholarly responsibilities will be commensurate with the candidate's experience, accomplishments, and career trajectory.
Required Qualifications
• MD, DO, or equivalent medical degree.
• Completion of an accredited Family Medicine residency program.
• Board certified or board eligible in Family Medicine.
• Eligible for unrestricted medical licensure in the State of Ohio.
• Demonstrated experience in scholarly activity relevant to academic family medicine, including clinical research, health services research, quality improvement, implementation science, population health, medical education scholarship, or a related discipline.
• Record of scholarly dissemination through peer-reviewed publications, presentations, educational products, or other evidence of academic contribution.
• Experience teaching, mentoring, or supervising medical students, residents, fellows, or other healthcare learners.
• Demonstrated ability to integrate clinical practice with scholarly activity.
• Eligibility for appointment at the Assistant Professor or Associate Professor rank within the College of Medicine.
Preferred Qualifications
• Established record of peer-reviewed publications demonstrating sustained scholarly productivity.
• Experience serving as principal investigator, co-principal investigator, co-investigator, project lead, or in an equivalent leadership role on research, quality improvement, implementation science, population health, health services research, or medical education initiatives.
• Experience obtaining, managing, or contributing to externally funded grants or contracts from governmental, foundation, industry, or other funding sources.
• Demonstrated leadership of interdisciplinary research, quality improvement, clinical innovation, or healthcare transformation initiatives.
• Experience translating scholarship into measurable improvements in clinical quality, patient outcomes, healthcare delivery, education, or population health.
• Evidence of regional or national recognition within an area of scholarly expertise.
• Experience mentoring trainees, junior faculty, researchers, or quality improvement teams.
• Demonstrated ability to develop and sustain an independent or collaborative program of scholarship while maintaining an active clinical practice in family medicine.
Faculty Defined
Clinical faculty (regardless of rank) - Persons with titles of assistant professor-clinical, associate professor-clinical, and professor-clinical. These faculty will have earned a Doctor of Medicine (MD), Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO), doctorate (PhD) or other terminal degree in the relevant field. Clinical faculty members are not eligible for tenure and are appointed for terms of three to five years. They may be reappointed to successive terms. Their primary career focus is the delivery of exemplary clinical care, which may also include teaching and/or research.
Tenure-Track faculty (regardless of rank) - Persons with the titles of assistant professor, associate professor, or professor who are eligible for tenure or who have obtained tenure. These faculty will have earned a doctorate (PhD), Doctor of Medicine (MD), Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO), or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study. Their primary career focus centers on research, service, and teaching. Tenure-track faculty with MD, DO, or MD/PhD degrees may also be involved in clinical care.
Research Faculty (regardless of rank) - Persons with the titles of research assistant professor, research associate professor, or research professor. These faculty will have earned a doctorate (PhD) or other terminal degree in the relevant field of study. Research faculty members are not eligible for tenure and are appointed for terms of one to five years. Their principal career focus is research.
The Ohio State University College of Medicine
The Ohio State University College of Medicine, with more than 5,000 learners, is the only academic medical center in central Ohio. Recognized as a Tier 1 school for research in the 2025–2026 U.S. News & World Report “Best Medical Schools” list, it ranks among the top 16 medical schools for research in the nation. It also remains in Tier 2 for primary care, further demonstrating its strength across the academic spectrum. Known for its innovative curriculum, cutting-edge research, and excellence in clinical care through The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, the college continues to advance its mission of education, discovery, and community impact. With more than 2,700 faculty across 20 clinical departments, eight basic science departments, and the School of Health and Rehabilitation Sciences, Ohio State is shaping the future of academic medicine - locally, nationally, and globally.
The Wexner Medical Center
The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center consists of The Ohio State University Health System, the College of Medicine, the Health Sciences Library, and the Faculty Group Practice. The Ohio State Wexner Medical Center is committed to providing world-class care. At the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center, we're proud to celebrate our 33rd consecutive year ranked on the U.S. News & World Report Best Hospitals list. This year, the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center has nine nationally ranked specialties out of 15, and four are selected as high performing. U.S. News & World Report consistently ranks the Ohio State Wexner Medical Center as the top hospital in Columbus. The Wexner Medical Center is rated as high performing in 17 out of 22 common procedures and conditions, including abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, aortic valve surgery, arrhythmia, COPD, colon cancer surgery, diabetes, gynecological cancer surgery, heart attack, heart failure, kidney failure, leukemia, lymphoma and myeloma, lung cancer surgery, pacemaker implantation, pneumonia, prostate cancer, spinal fusion, and transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
Our new hospital tower, scheduled to open in 2026, is the largest single facilities project ever undertaken at Ohio State. It’s designed to enhance a unified Ohio State Wexner Medical Center campus, providing world-class patient care, leading-edge research, and outstanding clinical training.
• 820 large, private rooms to elevate patient-centered care, nearly doubling the number of beds we have today
• Enhanced connections between the new inpatient hospital and the OSUCCC – James
• More than half an acre of terrace space and a quarter acre of green space for a small park
• 148 additional beds for patients of the OSUCCC – James

Job Details
Job Summary
This is a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level in the Department of Biology. The appointee is expected to establish a vigorous, externally funded research program, publish in peer-reviewed journals and teach effectively across the biology curriculum with special emphasis on Animal Physiology related courses. Additional responsibilities include service to the department, university, and discipline. The successful candidate will also involve undergraduate and graduate students in research. Preference will be given to candidates who have postdoctoral experience and whose research expertise can be leveraged towards advanced courses in Physiology utilizing molecular tools.
Special Note: We are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

1.Implement effective teaching strategies:
Teach Biology courses as assigned.
Develop course materials and contribute to curriculum development.
2.Maintain an active research agenda that includes publication of research papers in peer-reviewed journals and/or submission of research grants:
Conduct cutting edge research in the area of expertise.
Publish findings in peer-reviewed journals and present at professional conferences.
Supervise and mentor students.
Secure external funding through grants to support research initiatives.
3.Actively participate in academic service at the department, college, and university levels:
Serve the department, college and university as needed.
Assist in recruitment and retention of biology students.
Contribute to the academic and professional community through participation in relevant organizations and initiatives.
Minimum and Desired Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications:
A PhD in Biology or related field.
An established record of publications in peer-reviewed scientific journals that are listed by the Web of Science.
Willingness to develop and teach courses in area of research expertise and also Anatomy and Physiology, Upper-level Physiology.
Desired Qualifications:
Research background that can be leveraged towards advanced courses in Physiology.
Postdoctoral research experience.
Evidence of strong potential to secure external research funding.
Evidence of strong potential to mentor students in research.
Evidence of strong potential to teach high-quality courses across the biology curriculum.
Experience in presenting research results at high-profile conferences.
Supplemental Information
Key Competencies:
Strong ability to perform research in area of specialty.
Expected success in securing extramural funding.
Strong ability to teach high-quality Biology courses across the curriculum.
Demonstrated commitment to service to the university, profession, and community.
Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.
Physical Requirements: Able to lift 25 lbs and be able to perform a variety of physical tasks including lifting, bending, stooping, squatting, stair climbing and walking between buildings.
Job Conditions:
Standard academic work schedule, with occasional evening or weekend responsibilities to meet research, teaching, service, or administrative deadlines.
Position requires on-campus teaching with potential remote collaboration for research activities.

Teaching Philosophy
Curriculum Vita
Research Statement
Cover Letter
Three Letters of Recommendation

Department of Exercise Science
Open Rank: Tenure-Track Faculty Position:
The Department of Exercise Science (www.sph.sc.edu/exsc) at the University of South Carolina (USC) Arnold School of Public Health (ASPH – www.sph.sc.edu) invites applications for an open rank tenure-track faculty position to begin August 16, 2027. This position is part of a Presidential initiative for strategic hires in identified areas of interest across the university.
The successful candidate will have, or be able to develop, collaborative multi-disciplinary, translational research programs with a focus on biomechanics that complement or enhance research within the Department and across ASPH. Research programs of particular interest will have a primary emphasis on human health, performance, and/or injury.
The Department offers degrees at the undergraduate, masters, and doctoral level with programs in exercise science, athletic training, and physical therapy. The PhD program is consistently one of the top ranked programs in the US, and USC is among the top sport science universities in the US and the world. The Department currently serves approximately 1300 undergraduates and over 270 graduate students across all programs. Successful applicants will be expected to contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching and research, as well as supervise graduate students. The Department and Arnold School of Public Health have numerous researchers with a focus on exercise and health, performance, nutrition, endocrinology, metabolism, genetics, neuroscience, obesity, children’s health, and special populations. This position will be crucial for enhancing the capabilities in one or more of these areas.
Faculty members in the Department have established relationships with University Athletics, PRISMA Health, the Columbia VA Medical Center, US Special Operations Command, and numerous community partners and schools. The Department, School, and University also have excellent facilities to conduct everything from basic science and molecular work to applied interventions. Faculty members in the Department have access to well-equipped wet labs, a Clinical Exercise Research Center, and the state-of-the art Sport Science Lab.
USC is a research-intensive University and has been designated by the Carnegie Foundation as a doctoral institution with highest research activity. USC has also been designated a community engaged institution, making it one of only a few public universities to earn both the top-tier research classification and the community engagement classification from Carnegie. The university is in Columbia, South Carolina, the state capital and the center of a metropolitan area that is home to over 800,000 residents. The low cost of living in the Columbia metropolitan area, coupled with abundant recreational, cultural, and educational opportunities provides the opportunity for an excellent quality of life. Filled with historic homes and charming, diverse neighborhoods, Columbia is a city on the rise, noted by Thrillist website as one of eight cities with the cool appeal of Nashville or Portland. Jogging and walking paths line the downtown and riverfront greenway, with parks scattered throughout the rest of the city. The popularity of downtown living has sparked the growth of independent restaurants, coffee houses, wine bars, breweries, galleries, boutiques, and street fairs. Other Columbia highlights include: the Columbia Museum of Art with continuous high-profile traveling exhibits; the Nickelodeon art house cinema; the South Carolina State Museum with its planetarium, observatory, and 4-D movie theatre; the nationally recognized Riverbanks Zoo and Garden; and Lake Murray. Columbia has a lively local music scene as well as national entertainment tours that visit the Colonial Life Arena. Known for its college athletics teams as a member of the SEC, the city also hosts a minor league baseball team (the Columbia Fireflies). Centrally located, Columbia is two hours from the South Carolina coast and the Blue Ridge Mountains.
USC strives to create an inclusive, diverse community that facilitates our commitment to the communities that we serve. We seek opportunities to recruit, retain and promote individuals from traditionally underrepresented populations to further this vision. Our commitment to community engagement at the ASPH and university at-large is reflected by many programs and partnerships across campus.

An earned doctoral degree in exercise science, kinesiology, nutrition, neuroscience, biomedical engineering, or closely related fields.

Applicants for the Assistant Professor rank must demonstrate potential for: 1) outstanding research accomplishments, high-quality publications, and extramural funding to support a research program; and 2) for serving as an effective instructor and mentor.
Applicants for the Associate Professor rank must have a strong record of scholarship and funded research, plus at least five years of experience as an effective instructor, student mentor, and researcher by the start date of employment.

Job Summary:
The Angelo State University College of Arts and Humanities and Department of Visual and Performing Arts invites applications from qualified candidates to teach online and face-to-face courses in Video Game Art and Animation. The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Video Game Art and Animation is a new degree within the Department of Visual and Performing Arts. The ideal candidate will be able to help shape this degree for the next generation of video game artists. Applications will be accepted continuously and reviewed as instructional needs develop.
Ideal candidates will demonstrate strong abilities in art, creativity, design, and technology, supported by professional or academic experience in game design, technical art, real-time production, and game development processes. They should be capable of integrating visual arts with technology and teaching students how visual design, 3D modeling and asset creation, animation, lighting, materials, shaders, optimization, and interactive features function together in professional game-production settings.
They will also mentor students with backgrounds in graphic design, digital art, and traditional fine arts. The goal is to help students transfer their existing artistic knowledge into game development and build industry-focused technical art portfolios that demonstrate professional-level skills.
Essential Duties:
Teaching:
Instruct undergraduate studio art courses ranging from foundation drawing and design to courses involving Real-Time, Level Dressing, VFX for games, 2D Animation, 3D Modeling and Sculpting, Lighting, Rendering and Look Development. Other art courses as assigned.
Research and Creative Works:
Maintain a significant, ongoing studio practice with a record of professional accomplishments, such as solo and group exhibitions at local, regional, national or international levels.
Professional Service:
Serve on departmental and university committees. Manage studio facilities and assist in the coordination of the Video Game Art and Animation program. Participate in student recruitment and retention. Participate in departmental and Art Area meetings and events. Maintain regular office hours. Work collaboratively and productively with faculty colleagues to meet the needs of the student body.
Curriculum Development:
Lead or collaborate on revisions of the curriculum, integrating traditional skills with conceptual and interdisciplinary practices. Create curriculum for new courses within the VGAA curriculum to include both online and face-to-face modalities.
Mentorship:
Academic advising and mentoring BFA art students.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
Proficiency in 2D and 3D digital art tools used in contemporary game and animation production.
Proficiency in 3D asset creation and integration, procedural production techniques, lighting, materials, shaders, rigging, animation systems, artist-oriented scripting, AI-supported creative workflows, XR optimization, and other commonly used tools and processes associated with game development and real-time production.
Ability to recruit, retain students in the Video Game Art and Animation concentration.
Participate in departmental/Art Area meetings and events.
Maintain regular office hours.
Work collaboratively and productively with faculty colleagues to meet the needs of students and the Art Program.
Minimum Qualifications:
An MFA or PhD in game design, game programming, or a closely related discipline, including fields such as computer science, computer programming, or interactive design.
Preferred Qualifications:
Professional experience within the game industry is highly desirable.
At least two years of hands-on experience in game development using Unreal Engine production methods. Strong technical proficiency with Unreal Engine, Microsoft Visual Studio, C++, C#, Python, JavaScript, HLSL/GLSL, Verse, Advanced Blueprint Visual Scripting, computer graphics math, performance profiling, and specialized pipelines like Niagara VFX, animation and rendering.
Familiarity with industry-standard software, tools, and production workflows, including Autodesk Maya, Mudbox, Adobe Substance 3D, Adobe Creative Cloud, Blender, and ZBrush.
Physical Requirements:
Standing/sitting, bending, lifting, carrying as necessary per the job duties.

We are committed to ensuring that a qualified individual with a disability has the same rights and privileges in employment as non-disabled employees. If an accommodation is requested for the job application process, please contact our office at (325) 942-2168 or email us at hr@angelo.edu.

The department also offers a major and minor in commercial and investment real estate, as well as a certificate in financial planning. We are also launching a new M.S. Typically, the successful candidate will demonstrate interest and/or experience in teaching in at least two of the department’s areas of specialization—wealth management, banking and consumer finance, corporate finance, or commercial and investment real estate.

A candidate with a completed Ph.D. must have a recent and consistent record of publication in quality refereed journals. The Department of Finance and Economics also values candidates with industry experience and a commitment to community engagement. Candidates holding professional certifications (CFA®, CFP®, etc.) are preferred. The ideal candidate would also have a track record of community engagement and experiential learning that can create value for the department and for student learning experiences.

The position also requires service activities, including contributing to the assessment of student learning outcomes, and other service to the department, college, university, community, and profession. It is expected that the individual chosen for this position will possess a commitment to teaching excellence, demonstrated ability or capacity to produce quality scholarly academic research, a commitment to involvement in service to the university and the profession, excellent communication skills, and effective teamwork skills.

Enrollment in the finance degree has increased significantly in recent years, with over 700 students majoring in the discipline. The department also has minors in economics, commercial and investment real estate, and actuarial science and risk management along with a certificate in financial planning (CFP® Board Registered Program). Description of Work:
The Department of Special Education and Communication Disorders at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (UNL) is seeking applications for a tenure-leading Assistant or Associate Professor in Audiology. This 9-month (academic year) appointment will contribute to the department’s teaching and research missions, with an emphasis on developing a nationally and internationally recognized research program in audiology. This position will be located in Lincoln, Nebraska, with a projected start date of August 16, 2027.
The Department of Special Education and Communication Disorders at UNL is housed in a state-of-the-art facility in a newly expanded and renovated building. We have access to teaching and research equipment and resources that can help you launch a successful career. You will teach alongside our expert faculty in our spiral curriculum, where we integrate the expertise of our clinical and research faculty to create an environment where students are coached to make connections between research and practice. Our proximity to and collaborations with Boys Town National Research Hospital, Madonna Rehabilitation Hospital, UNL’s Center for Brain, Biology, and Behavior (CB3), and the University of Nebraska Medical Center may provide opportunities for you to build your program of research.
We are excited to welcome a new colleague at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor with expertise in audiology to join our collaborative and supportive faculty. We are especially interested in candidates whose work focuses on hearing and balance sciences, amplification and hearing aids, vestibular assessment and management, cognition and aging, or pediatric audiology. At the same time, we encourage applicants from a wide range of research areas who share our commitment to advancing knowledge and improving the lives of individuals with hearing and balance needs.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Build a collaborative research program that contributes to the advancement of audiology and has the potential to attract external support; teach undergraduate and graduate courses in areas of expertise; mentor and guide student research; and engage in professional service within the department, college, university, and broader community.
MORE ABOUT US
The Department of Special Education and Communication Disorders (https://cehs.unl.edu/secd) houses graduate programs in Audiology, Speech Language Pathology, and Special Education. SECD’s Audiology program is ranked among the top 20 audiology programs in the U.S. Faculty conduct cutting-edge research in global hearing health, communication access, hearing aids, cochlear implants, and neuroimaging. Our research thrives through interprofessional and interdepartmental collaboration, bringing together expertise from speech-language pathology, special education, engineering, athletics, psychology, and beyond.
The College of Education and Human Sciences strives to be a vibrant, welcoming, and caring community driven by our mission to enhance the lives of individuals, families, schools, and communities, and strengthening the relationships among them.
At the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, we’re proud to be consistently recognized by Forbes as a top employer, known for our welcoming and supportive work environment, commitment to professional growth, and outstanding benefits. UNL isn’t just a workplace, it’s a place to build your career and make a real impact in Nebraska.
Lincoln, Nebraska, is a vibrant and welcoming city of over 300,000 people that blends the cultural richness of a Big Ten university community with the affordability and ease of Midwestern living.

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor, Tenure-line Faculty, in Electrical and Computer Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Details
Description
The School of Engineering & Applied Science (SEAS) at the University of Virginia (UVa) seeks candidates for a tenure-eligible or tenured position in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. The primary responsibilities for this position include research, teaching at graduate and undergraduate levels, and service to the department, university, and professional community. The appointment rank and compensation will be commensurate with experience and qualifications.
The search is in the general area of neuroimaging, brain function and connectivity, and artificial intelligence, with applications to neuroscience and/or neuro-degenerative disorders. The school is especially interested in candidates who are interested in developing technologies that will enable a comprehensive understanding of the brain. Strategic integration of computational methods such as machine learning, signal processing, network theory, and a focus on application to neurological disorders including autism and Alzheimer’s disease, is desirable.
Example research areas include, but are not limited to
Neuroimaging
Investigation of brain function and connectivity at multiple scales
Brain machine interfaces, neural sensing and signal processing
Neuromodulation and stimulation
Neuroinformatics
Neuromorphic engineering
The Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) Department at the University of Virginia (UVA offers a vibrant environment for interdisciplinary research and collaboration, with strengths in areas such as machine learning, imaging, cyber-physical systems, embedded systems, communication networks, and energy systems. ECE at UVA emphasizes both foundational and applied research, preparing students for leadership in industry, academia, and government. Faculty members benefit from access to cutting-edge facilities and are encouraged to engage in research that addresses societal challenges. The close proximity with the School of Medicine offers rich opportunities for collaborations in the areas of Radiology, Neurology and Neuroscience, and Neurosurgery. Other collaborative opportunities include Biomedical Engineering, Psychology, and School of Data Science.
The University of Virginia's 2030 plan recognizes the Brain and Neuroscience as a major societal challenge and an opportunity for multidisciplinary work that draws on our existing strengths. In partnership the Provost and the deans of various schools are making multiple coordinated faculty recruitments to strengthen the research community focusing on Brain and Neuroscience across the University. Recruits will receive support from the Provost and from their school and will participate in the Brain and Neuroscience Initiative. This is part of a major Grand Challenges research investment of over $50M in Brain and Neuroscience.
This position is based in Charlottesville at our principal location. UVA is a highly selective undergraduate and graduate institution that annually ranks as one of the premiere public universities in the United States, with one of the highest graduation rates in the nation. UVA is situated in Charlottesville, Virginia, a picturesque and vibrant small city consistently recognized as one of the nation's top places to reside. UVA's location offers proximity to Washington D.C., enriching opportunities for collaboration and engagement with numerous federal organizations. More information about the city, the school, faculty benefits and other topics can be found at https://hr.virginia.edu/careers-uva/why-uva.
Qualifiations
Candidates must have received a doctorate or equivalent in electrical engineering, computer science, biomedical engineering or related areas by the start of their appointment. Evidence of a commitment to high-impact scholarship, funded research, undergraduate- and graduate-level teaching and advising excellence, professional and university service, and mentoring are expected.
In conjunction with these positions, senior graduate students are eligible and encouraged to consider the UVA Engineering Rising Scholars program. This program is designed to encourage early-career scholars to pursue a career in academia by supporting their postdoctoral work before beginning in a tenure-track position at the University of Virginia. Detailed information and application instructions are available at https://engineering.virginia.edu/rising-scholars-postdoctoral-program.
Application Instructions
Apply for this position in Interfolio. Provide the following in PDF format:
Cover letter that summarizes your areas of research/scholarship, and areas of potential collaboration at the University of Virginia. To help us organize our review of applications, please also specifically list your primary areas of research in boldface at the top of your letter
Curriculum vitae
A statement describing your current research, future directions, and broader impacts;
A statement describing your teaching and mentoring practices, especially in regard to a residential learning environment marked by the free and collegial exchange of ideas;
A statement describing demonstrated contributions to fostering inclusive practices that create climates in which all stakeholders can achieve their maximum potential (please focus on skills and experience, not beliefs and opinions)
A single file that includes two research papers that best represent your work
You will also request 3-5 references directly in Interfolio by providing names and contact information in the application. These reference requests will be generated immediately once you submit your application.
Review of applications will begin on October 19, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. The University will perform background checks on all new faculty hires prior to making a final offer of employment.
For questions about these positions, please contact Mathews Jacob, Professor, Electrical and Computer Engineering at mjacob@virginia.edu.

jobs.title: Open Rank Tenured/Tenure Track Professor of Data Science in Natural Language Processing
jobs.description:
Job Details
Description
The University of Virginia School of Data Science is seeking exceptional candidates for an open-rank tenured or tenure-track faculty position in Natural Language Processing (NLP), with particular emphasis on Large Language Models (LLMs). This search prioritizes faculty making foundational and methodological contributions that improve the understanding or capabilities of language models. We seek a scholar with deep technical expertise in advancing language models, including their architectures, learning objectives, data and training methods, adaptation and post-training, reasoning, evaluation, and efficient implementation. We especially welcome candidates who connect language model research with other areas of data science and with important domains across the University. A successful candidate will join a collaborative faculty community committed to research excellence, innovative teaching, interdisciplinary partnership, and the responsible advancement of data science and AI. Faculty have the opportunity to shape a rapidly evolving field while leveraging the strengths of one of the nation's leading public research universities, with exceptional opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and scholarly impact.
Qualifiations
We welcome candidates whose scholarship advances NLP and language modeling through foundational and methodological research. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to:
Foundations, training, and efficiency of language models, including architectures, learning objectives, data curation, pretraining and post-training, scaling, long-context modeling and memory, continual learning, and efficient training and inference.
Reasoning, knowledge, and agentic AI, including reasoning and planning, tool use, retrieval-augmented and knowledge-grounded generation, symbolic methods, autonomous and multi-agent systems, and human-agent collaboration.
Multimodal and grounded language intelligence, including vision-language, speech- and audio-language, video-language, cross-modal learning, and world models.
Multilingual and human-centered NLP, including low-resource methods, language diversity, linguistic and cognitive foundations, dialogue and interactive systems, and accessible and inclusive language technologies.
Language models integrated with data science and domain discovery, including methods that connect language with structured, temporal, scientific, or multimodal data in areas such as science, engineering, health, education, social sciences, and public policy.
These areas are illustrative, and candidates are not expected to work across all of them. We are most interested in applicants with intellectual depth, original contributions, and a compelling long-term vision for advancing NLP and language model research.
Candidates must have earned, or be on track to earn, a PhD in Data Science, Computer Science, Computational Linguistics, Linguistics, Information Science, Statistics, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or a closely related field by August 2027 or appointment start date. A commitment to advancing the University's mission is essential for all candidates (https://provost.virginia.edu/faculty-handbook/mission-statement-university-virginia).
When applying, candidates should detail their research expertise and interests, their instructional experience, preferred teaching domain, and other scholarly interests. Candidates should have a strong publication record in leading peer-reviewed NLP, computational linguistics, and AI venues. Examples include ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, TACL, Computational Linguistics, as well as other comparably selective venues appropriate to the work. Candidates for senior ranks (associate and full with tenure) must have a demonstrated record of excellence in research, teaching, and advising, in data science and/or closely related fields, and must have established a national/international reputation for contribution to the field in methodology, application, and impact. Candidates for assistant rank (tenure-track) must demonstrate the potential for excellence in methodological development and scientific impact in data science or a related field and have prior experience in educational-related activities.
Application Instructions
Complete an application online and attach:
A current Curriculum Vitae or Resume.
A Cover Letter that addresses your experience and qualifications for this position and your interest in data science.
A research statement that describes your past research endeavors and contributions, as well as your future research goals (1-3 pages).
A teaching statement that describes your teaching and mentoring experiences, and how they align with the UVA’s mission statement (https://provost.virginia.edu/faculty-handbook/mission-statement-university-virginia). This statement should focus on your past or planned educational activities and how you see data science education evolving over the next decade (1-3 pages).
Three reference letters or detailed contact information for three references.
If available, reviews & course evaluations from up to 3 educational courses, seminars, and/or short courses.
Review of applicants will begin on or around December 1st, 2026, and the positions will remain open until filled. Rank will be commensurate with academic and industry experience. Appointments are available on 9-month contracts.
About the School
Founded in 2019, the School of Data Science at the University of Virginia (UVA) - the first of its kind in the nation - advances discovery, innovation, and societal impact through collaborative, open, and responsible data science research and education. The School brings together expertise across business, computation, engineering, humanities, law, mathematics, social sciences, statistics, and law to address complex, real world challenges. Its academic offerings include a B.S. in Data Science, an undergraduate minor, residential and online M.S. in Data Science programs, and a Ph.D. in Data Science, all designed to prepare students for a rapidly evolving data driven world. UVA researchers have access to the Afton and Rivanna high-performance computing systems, which provide tens of thousands of CPU cores, more than eight petabytes of storage, and NVIDIA A100, H200, and B200 GPUs. SDS also acquired additional H200 and B200 clusters to support its faculty’s research and education.
For questions about the application process please contact Jennifer Kirkham, Manager for Faculty Affairs at the School of Data Science, at sdsfacultyaffairs@virginia.edu. For more information about the School of Data Science, see Faculty Jobs — School of Data Science.
The selected candidate will be required to complete a background check at time of offer per University Policy.
For more information about UVA and the Charlottesville community please see http://www.virginia.edu/life/charlottesville and https://embarkcva.com/.
UVA is in beautiful Charlottesville with easy access to the Blue Ridge Mountains, the eastern shore and the nation's Capital. Charlottesville is consistently ranked as one of the best places to live in the U.S. (e.g., see liveability.com) with access to outdoor activities, vibrant culture, and excellent schools and restaurants.
For more information on the benefits available to faculty at UVA, visit https://provost.virginia.edu/subsite/faculty-development and hr.virginia.edu/benefits.

The University of Virginia School of Data Science is a leader in preparing students, advancing research, and developing the intellectual foundations that underpin the age of artificial intelligence. About the University of Georgia:
Chartered by the state of Georgia in 1785, the University of Georgia is the birthplace of public higher education in America and is the state’s flagship university (https://www.uga.edu/). The proof is in our more than 240 years of academic and professional achievements and our continual commitment to higher education. UGA is currently ranked among the top 20 public universities in U.S. News & World Report. The University’s main campus is located in Athens, approximately 65 miles northeast of Atlanta, with extended campuses in Atlanta, Griffin, Gwinnett, and Tifton. UGA employs approximately 3,100 faculty and more than 7,700 full-time staff. The University’s enrollment exceeds 41,000 students including over 31,000 undergraduates and over 10,000 graduate and professional students. Academic programs reside in 19 schools and colleges, including our newly established School of Medicine.
About the College/Unit/Department:
The UGA Carl Vinson Institute of Government – Who We Are
As a Public Service and Outreach unit at the University of Georgia, the UGA Institute of Government contributes directly to the university’s overarching public service mission of improving people’s lives by helping to create jobs and prosperity, developing leaders, and addressing critical issues. This public service mission, and the Institute of Government’s role in its success, is at the heart of UGA’s land-grant and sea-grant mission to serve the State of Georgia and its residents.
We have a wide range of experts who inform, inspire, and innovate every day so that governments, large and small, can be more efficient and responsive to their citizens, address current and emerging challenges, and serve the public with excellence. We are uniquely positioned to provide impartial support to local governments and state agencies and convene multi-disciplinary and intragovernmental groups to plan for and address many of the challenges faced by communities across Georgia.
Our areas of expertise and focus include workforce and economic development; infrastructure and community resilience; government operations and organizational effectiveness; measuring and reporting on impact and outcomes; building skills, knowledge and capacity of government leaders and teams; and maximizing technology and data for governments and their leaders.
Whether it is through our award-winning PROPEL (Planning Rural Opportunities for Prosperity and Economic Leadership) program for rural communities, our CyberArch student program that helps Georgia communities increase their cybersecurity, our efforts to build a visionary plan for military and community partnerships to spur economic prosperity and resilient infrastructure, our financial management certificate program to build the capacity of public officials, or hosting educational events about e-mobility strategies for local governments …. We Know Georgia. Fulfilling our land-grant and sea-grant mission to serve the State of Georgia is more than a project. It’s our purpose.
We are growing and excited to add individuals to our team who share our commitment to public service – building stronger communities, inspiring economic resilience, and improving quality of life for communities across Georgia and beyond.
Our Culture – How We Operate
We disseminate knowledge through research, scholarship, and instruction. We collaborate internally across our areas of expertise and across the university with academic researchers to bring best practices and expert insights to the governments and communities we serve. We are committed to fielding a team of experts who have a variety of professional and academic experiences and are grounded in our culture of excellence and approach our work with Georgia’s governments in a comprehensive and objective fashion.

As the 4th largest public college of education in the country and the 3rd largest college at UGA, the Mary Frances Early College of Education (MFE COE) improves the lives of residents of Georgia and beyond through our instruction, research, and service. The MFE COE is a comprehensive college with disciplines focused on teacher preparation, counseling and human development, communication sciences, human movement sciences, career development, student affairs, and educational administration and policy. We place significant emphasis on graduate education with approximately 40% of our students at the graduate level, making us the second largest college at UGA with respect to graduate education.
ETAP has contributed to this stature locally, nationally, and internationally. The department is characterized by critical, forward-thinking research and innovative, dynamic teaching. ETAP is committed to making equity, access, and belonging visible in its courses, programs, policies, and practice. Our outreach and research include a variety of multifaceted collaborations, including those with local school districts and local community-based informal education projects, as well as projects that extend across the state of Georgia, the United States, and a variety of international contexts. Information about the department is available at https://coe.uga.edu/directory/educational-theory-and-practice/.
The Elementary Education program at UGA, which includes Early Childhood Education, has been ranked among the nation’s top 10 elementary education programs by U.S. News and World Report for more than a decade. Our mission in the Elementary Education program is to blend theory and practice grounded in our shared philosophy of critical pedagogy. Upon program completion, we expect our students to demonstrate teaching competencies related to habits of reflexive practice, integrating scholarship and research, engaging in professional collaboration, and appreciating and supporting multiple backgrounds and perspectives. These elements of thought and action are viewed as key to supporting critically informed and equitable teacher decision-making. The Elementary Education program is designed to offer theoretically and clinically rich experiences in diverse environments. By the end of the program, teachers are prepared to enact these commitments as leaders in their classrooms, schools, and communities.

Job Description
The Department of Computational, Engineering and Mathematical Sciences invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Cyber Engineering Technology (CET) beginning Spring/Summer 2027.
We seek an innovative educator and scholar whose expertise lies at the intersection of electronics, embedded systems, and cybersecurity. The successful candidate will contribute to the continued development of our Cyber Engineering Technology program while fostering strong collaboration with the Department's Electronics Systems Technology (ESET) and Cybersecurity, Computer Science and Mathematics programs as appropriate.
A&M-SA is a fast-growing comprehensive regional university with over 7,500 students. It is part of the statewide Texas A&M University System, A&M-SA is located on 694 acres in south San Antonio and serves a multi-cultural student body, offering academic programs that meet regional needs. The campus, with Mudéjar style buildings and contemporary facilities that leverage technology to enhance the student experience, embraces the spirit of San Antonio’s rich culture. Self-reported demographic data indicate 60% of students are the first generation in their family in college, and 66% women. We seek to recruit faculty that enhance the breadth, depth, and quality of our students' educational experience.We are committed to the success of first-generation college students and military veterans.In this context applicants should address, in their cover letter, how their life experiences, work history, professional engagement, and relevant community engagement will contribute to the success of our students, and what the applicants' plans are for serving our student population.
Areas of interest include, but are not limited to:
Hardware and embedded systems security, including secure hardware architectures, firmware, trusted computing, FPGA security, and hardware-assisted cryptography.
Internet of Things (IoT) and edge computing security, including embedded devices, wireless communications, industrial IoT, and secure sensing platforms.
Cyber-physical systems and critical infrastructure security, including industrial control systems (ICS), operational technology (OT), smart manufacturing, robotics, transportation, water, energy, and other intelligent infrastructure.
Applied cybersecurity for electronic systems, including hardware assurance, secure system design, vulnerability analysis, cyber resilience, and AI-enabled cyber defense.
Applicants with experience integrating cybersecurity principles into electronics, embedded systems, automation, or intelligent infrastructure are especially encouraged to apply.
The Department is committed to preparing graduates who can design, build, secure, and operate modern cyber-enabled engineering systems. The Cyber Engineering Technology program emphasizes applied learning through laboratories, project-based instruction, undergraduate research, industry collaboration, and experiential education. Faculty are encouraged to pursue interdisciplinary research spanning cybersecurity, engineering, artificial intelligence, robotics, intelligent infrastructure, digital twins, and resilient cyber-physical systems.
Salary: Commensurate with experience and qualifications.
Responsibilities:
Teach undergraduate courses primarily in cyber engineering technology and electronics systems engineering technology. Ability to teach undergraduate and graduate level courses in cybersecurity and computer science as appropriate.
Contribute to impactful research and mentoring of both undergraduate and graduate students.
Contribute to the service mission of the university.
Required Education and Experience:
An earned Ph.D. or Doctor of Engineering in Cyber-Engineering or a related field by the time of the appointment. The candidate’s expertise and experience must focus on the security of hardware, IoT, embedded or cyber-physical systems.
Candidates with ABD status will be considered if the requirements for the Ph.D. degree are completed before the appointment begins (degree conferral may happen later).
A commitment to teaching excellence, especially at the undergraduate level, using hands-on experiential learning methods.
Demonstrated potential of scholarly activity with an ability to secure external funding.
Strong written and oral communication skills.
An entrepreneurial mindset with a focus on contributing to department and university growth.
Demonstration of excellent written and oral communication skills.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Jacksonville State University
Assistant Professor, Biology (Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy)
The Department of Biology at Jacksonville State University invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy. Jacksonville State University is committed to excellence in teaching, student engagement, and experiential learning. The successful candidate will contribute to the department's instructional mission through teaching, mentoring, scholarly activity, and service.
The faculty member will be expected to teach undergraduate and graduate courses that support the biology curriculum, including general biology for majors and non-majors, comparative vertebrate anatomy, and other courses aligned with the candidate's expertise. The successful candidate will demonstrate a commitment to student-centered instruction and active learning approaches that promote student success and engagement.
In addition to teaching responsibilities, the faculty member will be expected to develop and maintain a productive scholarly agenda in comparative vertebrate anatomy, organismal biology, evolutionary morphology, or a closely related field. Research activities that involve undergraduate and graduate student participation are strongly encouraged.
Some departmental funding to support establishment of a research program is provided.
About The Department
The department currently maintains a variety of specialized facilities, as well as traditional and modern instrumentation, in support of student/faculty research.
In recent years, student/faculty research has been supported by extramural funding through the National Science Foundation, National Institutes of Health, NASA, Alabama Environmental Council, Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, U. S. Forest Service and other agencies/groups.
Essential Functions
Teach undergraduate and graduate biology courses, including comparative vertebrate anatomy and related laboratory courses.
Teach introductory biology courses for majors and non-majors as needed by the department.
Employ evidence-based and active learning pedagogies that support student success and retention.
Develop and maintain laboratory experiences that enhance student learning and scientific inquiry.
Establish and sustain a scholarly research program appropriate for a teaching-focused institution.
Mentor undergraduate and graduate students through independent research projects, internships, and other experiential learning opportunities.
Advise students regarding academic progress, career pathways, and professional development opportunities.
Participate in curriculum development, assessment activities, and accreditation efforts.
Maintain appropriate records and documentation related to teaching, student assessment, and scholarly activities.
Contribute to departmental, college, and university service activities.
Develop collaborative relationships with professional organizations and individuals within the discipline.
Seek external funding opportunities to support research and student engagement activities when appropriate.
Position Requirements
Earned Ph.D. in Biology, Zoology, Comparative Anatomy, Evolutionary Biology, Organismal Biology, or a closely related discipline by the date of appointment.
Demonstrated knowledge of comparative vertebrate anatomy, anatomical nomenclature, and contemporary approaches used to address questions in organismal and anatomical biology.
Evidence of potential for excellence in undergraduate teaching.
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively in English, both orally and in writing.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with students, faculty, staff, and external professional communities.
Basic computer proficiency and ability to utilize instructional technologies.
Ability to support and mentor students from diverse academic backgrounds.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience teaching undergraduate laboratory and lecture courses.
Experience utilizing active learning, course-based undergraduate research experiences (CUREs), or other high-impact educational practices.
Experience with specimen- and/or dissection-based instructions
Postdoctoral research experience.
Evidence of scholarly productivity and potential for developing a sustainable research program involving undergraduate and graduate students.
Experience pursuing or obtaining extramural funding.
Experience advising or mentoring undergraduate and graduate students.
Applicants must submit a cover letter, resume or CV, teaching philosophy, research statement, and all earned unofficial transcripts to be considered for the position. Official transcripts will be required upon hire.
The salary range for this position is $60,204.00 - $66,330.00 based on years of direct experience.
This position has an anticipated start date of August 2, 2027.
About Jacksonville State University
Located in the Appalachian foothills of northeast Alabama, midway between Birmingham and Atlanta, Jax State is home to more than 10,400 students representing 63 countries. As a learning-centered university, it strives to challenge students academically in a responsive environment, meeting their educational, career and personal goals. As an academic institution, it seeks to produce broadly educated graduates prepared for global engagement. As a public, comprehensive university, it promotes excellence in scholarly and service activities consistent with its academic and professional strengths. For a complete list of Goals, Core Values and Strategies to fulfill this Mission, go to the JSU Strategic Plan home page.
Academically Jax State offers 113 academic programs and concentrations, including bachelor's, master's, post-baccalaureate, doctoral and advanced certificate programs in a variety of disciplines that prepare graduates for meaningful careers and ongoing education. More than 40 online programs are offered. The University features six colleges on its 459-acre campus – Arts, Humanities and Sciences; Business and Industry; Education and Professional Studies; Health Professions and Wellness; Social and Behavioral Sciences; and Library. Most academic programs have discipline-specific accreditations, a reflection of their quality and JSU’s commitment to excellence.
Jacksonville State University Commitment
Jacksonville State University seeks faculty who are dedicated to creating engaging learning environments, fostering student achievement, and contributing to the University's mission of providing high-quality educational opportunities. Successful candidates will demonstrate a commitment to teaching excellence, student mentorship, scholarly engagement, and service to the University and broader scientific community.

Equal Employment Opportunity: Jax State is an Equal Employment and Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

We seek an engaged teacher-scholar whose research addresses fundamental or applied questions in ecology, evolution, organismal biology, conservation science, wildlife and fisheries biology, natural resource management, or related disciplines.
