We welcome applicants employing field-based, laboratory, computational, quantitative, or interdisciplinary approaches that enhance opportunities for student involvement in research and experiential learning.
The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate education by teaching courses such as Introductory Biology, Ecology and Evolution, organismal biology, field biology, and specialized courses aligned with their expertise. The successful applicant will be expected to establish an active research agenda that engages and mentors both undergraduate and graduate students, produces scholarly publications, pursues external funding, and contributes to the academic mission of the department, college, and university through teaching, research, and service.

Teach Introductory Biology, Evolution and Ecology, an organismal or field-based course, and courses in their specialty supporting the B.S. and M.S. Biology Programs, the Wildlife Ecology Certificate, and the emerging Natural Resources Management Program.
Establish and maintain a funded research program in biology that incorporates undergraduate and graduate students. Opportunity to collaborate across disciplines within the program, college, and university. Pursue scholarly activity, including peer-reviewed publications.

Demonstrated record or potential of excellence in scholarship with peer-reviewed research publications.

Faculty/Division: Temerty Faculty of Medicine

Hospital Affiliation: Sunnybrook Health Science Centre
Campus: St. George (Downtown Toronto)
Existing Vacancy: Yes
Description:
The Department Surgery, Division of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery at the Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre and the University of Toronto are inviting applications for the position of an academic Plastic and Reconstructive Surgeon specializing in craniofacial and soft tissue reconstruction/trauma plastic surgery.
The effective date of this appointment is July 1, 2027, but can be flexible depending on the candidate.
The successful candidate will join a dynamic and collegial team of plastic and reconstructive surgeons with a major focus on craniofacial surgery and trauma reconstruction. The successful candidate will also participate in medical student, resident, and plastic surgery fellow education at the University of Toronto. The successful candidate will have an academic role of Surgeon Teacher or Investigator.
The successful candidate must have completed specialized fellowship training in craniofacial surgery. Solid expertise in the reconstruction of complex soft tissue defects is also required for this position. Expertise in the management of skin cancers is also an asset. The successful candidate will share in a 1:7 plastic surgery on call pool. Evidence of excellence in teaching and research is required. The candidate’s application should demonstrate excellence in academic activities (research, quality improvement, education). The successful candidate should have a strong research track record, preferably resulting in a M.Sc. or PhD degree.
The candidate must be eligible for appointment at the University of Toronto at the academic rank of Assistant/Associate/Full Professor and will participate in the educational programs and academic mission of the University of Toronto Division of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery as a full-time member. The candidate must hold an MD and FRCSC (or equivalent specialist designation) qualification in plastic surgery and be eligible for certification with the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (or hold international equivalent), and licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario.
Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre is one of Canada’s largest hospitals and a leader in clinical and research activities. Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre is a fully affiliated academic health sciences facility of the University of Toronto and home to one of the University’s three academies for undergraduate education. Sunnybrook has an international reputation for clinical excellence in research and is an acknowledged academic leader. The Sunnybrook Research Institute hosts well established programs in basic, applied and clinical research occupying over 250,000 square feet of state-of-the-art infrastructure with annual peer reviewed grants of $100 million dollars.
The Division of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery at Sunnybrook provides all aspects of plastic surgery reconstruction, including hand surgery, peripheral nerve surgery, microsurgical reconstruction, craniofacial surgery, skin cancer care, and wound reconstruction. The Division performs at least 1000 emergent and elective cases per annum with over >6000 clinical visits per year. Many of the patients come through the Tory Regional Trauma Centre ensuring a complex case mix of trauma reconstruction.
Annual salary will be between the range of $300,000 - $350,000, commensurate with qualifications and experience. This estimate is based on fee for service billings.
Please submit a letter of interest including an academic plan for the first 3-5 years of practice along with a brief EDI statement, curriculum vitae, and the names of three referees and their contact information by October 23, 2026 to:
Dr. Laura Snell
Division Head, Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery
Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre
Laura.Snell@sunnybrook.ca
For more information about the Temerty Faculty of Medicine/Department of Surgery and the Department of Surgery, Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre, please visit http://surgery.utoronto.ca and https://sunnynet.ca.

jobs.description:
Assistant Professor- Tenure System
Job # 1167599
Posting Snapshot:
The School of Social Work is seeking candidates for a nine-month Assistant Professor in the tenure system to join our team.
Reports to:
School of Social Work Director
Position Summary:
Michigan State University actively promotes a dynamic research and learning environment in which qualified individuals of differing perspectives and cultural backgrounds pursue academic goals with mutual respect and shared inquiry.
The School of Social Work is seeking candidates for an Assistant Professor position in the tenure stream. We seek candidates with a well-defined research agenda and the potential to make meaningful contributions to the field through creative, innovative, and rigorous scholarship. We encourage applications from candidates with research interests that build upon our four core areas of research expertise: health and aging; marginalized youth and families; sexual and gender minority health; and violence and violence prevention. We also welcome candidates with research interests that expand our School’s areas of expertise, including candidates whose research uses innovative research methods to address emerging issues in social work. Candidates should show promise for securing external research funding, producing high-quality scholarship, and contributing to our vibrant intellectual community. Position expectations include teaching across the social work curriculum, at both undergraduate and graduate levels, mentoring students, and participating in our school community. The successful candidate will have opportunities to collaborate with faculty across the university and participate in interdisciplinary research initiatives. Candidates who have experience promoting intellectual debates around a diversity of viewpoints and perspectives are especially encouraged to apply.
School Statement:
The MSU School of Social Work, within the College of Social Science, is dedicated to educating students for ethical, competent, responsive, and innovative social work practice, and to conducting and disseminating high quality research that improves the well-being of the most vulnerable in society. Our teaching, research, and outreach synergistically promote social justice, positive change, and solutions to the problems facing a broad cross section of individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities. More than 650 students are enrolled in our CSWE- accredited BASW and MSW programs, and our PhD program.
Minimum Qualifications:
An earned doctorate in Social Work or a related field by the date of employment
A beginning record of scholarly productivity, evidenced by peer-reviewed publications, scholarly presentations, research funding activity, or other relevant scholarly contributions.
A clearly articulated research agenda with demonstrated potential to make meaningful contributions to social work knowledge.
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively in writing and orally in scholarly, teaching, and professional settings.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively in research, teaching, or professional settings.
Commitment to engaged teaching, active learning, and student advancement, as evidenced by experience as instructor of record, teaching assistant, guest lecturer, or similar experience facilitating learning.
Preferred Qualifications:
MSW from an accredited School of Social Work
A record of success in acquiring extramural research funding
Teaching experience with undergraduate and graduate students across course delivery modalities (in-person, online synchronous, online asynchronous).
Candidates who have experience promoting intellectual debates around a diversity of viewpoints and perspectives are especially encouraged to apply.
This is a 9-month tenure-system position beginning September 2027. Salary for this position is negotiable and commensurate with qualifications and experiences. Michigan State University offers an excellent selection of benefits; please see www.hr.msu.edu for more information.
Required Application Documents:
Complete applications must include:
a cover letter detailing the reasons for applying for the position and how your research and/or background fits with the position description;
a curriculum vitae;
a 1-page research statement;
a 1-page teaching statement;
Names and contact information for three professional (3) references. The unit solicits reference letters in PageUp using the names/contact info the applicants provide. Note: applications cannot be reviewed until all three reference letters have been received.
Special Instructions
Applications must be submitted to the MSU Applicant Page at https://careers.msu.edu. Enter 1167599 in the search bar. We will begin reviewing applications Fall 2026 and will continue until position is filled. For questions, please contact Dr. Pilar Horner, phorner@msu.edu.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor
jobs.description:
Johns Hopkins University's School of Government and Policy seeks to recruit multiple tenure-track faculty in multiple disciplines and fields of study, including (but not limited to) political science, law, sociology, history, philosophy, computer science, and economics.
While searching broadly, we have a particular interest in faculty conducting research on the following topics of inquiry:
Cities and Communities: State and local policymaking and implementation. Applications are encouraged from candidates in civil engineering, economics, history, law, sociology, political science, public administration, or urban planning, with research interests including local governance, state capacity, urban innovation, housing and real estate, public education and school choice, transportation and land use, or local finance and budgeting.
Frontier AI: The implications of highly advanced AI for government and society. Applications are encouraged from candidates from a wide range of disciplines including computer science, economics, philosophy, law, political science cognitive science, and sociology. Research interests might include: AI alignment and governance; the government, societal, and labor market impacts of and adaptation to AI; the use of AI to simulate and design policy interventions; regulatory theory and innovation; institutional design and innovation; and AI evaluation, auditing and verification.
Political Philosophy and Theory: Ambitious, foundational, big-picture political philosophy and/or political theory with direct relevance to government and policy, advancing the school's mission of shoring up and renewing the core institutions of liberal democracy. Applications are encouraged from candidates who are problem-focused and syncretistic, drawing on different conceptual, methodological, and empirical approaches and orienting themselves outward from philosophy/theory toward the world, with particular interest in candidates whose work intersects with or complements other parts of the School's research strengths.
Public-Sector Innovation and Management: How governments and other public-sector organizations function, why they succeed or fail, and how to change them to more effectively solve public problems. Applications are encouraged from candidates in the social sciences, management, history, organizational behavior, psychology, urban planning, operations research, industrial and systems engineering, management science, public management, or public policy. Research interests might include: institutional reform and organizational change; public innovation and problem solving; public-sector management, budgeting, procurement, contracting, and operations; state capacity and bureaucratic performance; organizational structure, behavior, learning, and culture; the adoption and management of technology in government, including the organizational challenges of effective implementation and how technologies affect public-sector organizations, policy, and governance.
Regulation, Bureaucracy, and Public Administration: Why governments so often fail to deliver what policies promise, and what institutional redesigns would enable them to do so. Applications are encouraged from candidates in political science, law, public administration, history, sociology, or other fields whose work is changing the terms of academic and public debate. Research interests might include: the politics of civil service and personnel systems; federalism and the implementation of large public programs; intergovernmental relations; regulation, enforcement, and capture; administrative procedure and policy analysis; or state capacity more broadly.
Across all these searches, we seek candidates who can work and learn across disciplines and take seriously the need to improve government effectiveness. We welcome candidates who have worked within public-sector and policymaking institutions and alongside government reformers from across the political spectrum. We are also interested in candidates who wish to investigate the challenges and opportunities of governing and deploying artificial intelligence.
About the School of Government and Policy
Anchored at the Hopkins Bloomberg Center in the heart of Washington, D.C., the School of Government and Policy will be a hub of discovery, collaboration, and impact. At a time of political, social, and technological upheaval, this new school will support and inform scholarly and practical efforts to build a more effective government and solve complex policy challenges. The school will scrutinize institutional reforms that have the potential to improve government operations, examine the potential for advancing technologies to transform government workforces and operations, develop novel approaches to multidisciplinary education and experiential learning, and foster vital dialogue and engagement across a wide range of worldviews, backgrounds, and epistemologies.
Similar to JHU's other academic divisions, the School of Government and Policy will be grounded in a commitment to both world-class research and exceptional education. It will prepare the next generation of policy and public sector leaders to advance evidence-based solutions to society's greatest challenges through innovative approaches that: 1) embed science, data, and technology in curricula; 2) give students the tools required to think strategically and creatively about government and policy innovations; and 3) emphasize the critical need for cross-functional skills and capabilities at all levels of government and in bridging public, non-profit, and industry sectors.
We are building a community of scholars, experts, and leaders from a wide range of disciplines who embrace intellectual pluralism--with the intention not merely of representing different perspectives and ways of understanding, but of putting these differences to good use. We welcome applications from scholars who challenge conventional thinking through rigorous inquiry.
Over the course of its founding years, the school will grow to encompass 35 full-time faculty members with expertise that spans both theoretical and applied approaches to public policy and government. During this founding period, additional hires will be made with other units across the University, yielding an even larger and more integrated tenured and tenure-track faculty.
Qualifications
Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in an appropriate field or J.D. by the time their appointment begins. Candidates must have demonstrated an ability to conduct outstanding independent research and show promise for excellent teaching, mentoring, and public engagement.
Application Instructions
Interested applicants should submit a cover letter, CV, two writing samples, and three letters of recommendation. Applications will be considered on a rolling basis and should be received by October 25, 2026 for full consideration. Interested candidates should submit their applications via Interfolio.
Dependent upon discipline, rank, and other factors listed below, the overall expected salary range for this position is $100,000 to $200,000.
Salary Range
The referenced salary range represents the minimum and maximum salaries for this position and is based on Johns Hopkins University's good faith belief at the time of posting. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. The actual compensation offered to the selected candidate may vary and will ultimately depend on multiple factors, which may include the successful candidate's geographic location, skills, work experience, internal equity, market conditions, education/training and other factors, as reasonably determined by the University.
Total Rewards
Johns Hopkins offers a total rewards package that supports our employees' health, life, career and retirement. More information can be found here: https://hr.jhu.edu/benefits-worklife/.
Equal Opportunity Employer
The Johns Hopkins University is committed to equal opportunity for its faculty, staff, and students. To that end, the university does not discriminate on the basis of sex, gender, marital status, pregnancy, race, color, ethnicity, national origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status or other legally protected characteristics. The university is committed to providing qualified individuals access to all academic and employment programs, benefits and activities on the basis of demonstrated ability, performance and merit without regard to personal factors or demographic characteristics that are irrelevant to the program involved.
Pre-Employment Information
If you are interested in applying for employment with Johns Hopkins University and require special assistance or accommodation during any part of the pre-employment process, please contact the HR Business Services Office at jhurecruitment@jhu.edu. For TTY users, call via Maryland Relay or dial 711. For more information about workplace accommodations at Johns Hopkins University for disabilities, medical conditions (including medical conditions related to pregnancy or childbirth), accessibility, or religious reasons, please visit accessibility.jhu.edu.
Background Checks
After receiving a conditional offer, the successful candidate(s) for this position will be subject to a pre-employment background check including education verification. When deciding whether a candidate's conviction history is job-disqualifying, the University considers the nature and gravity of the offense, the time that has passed since the conviction, and the nature of the job being sought.
EEO is the Law
https://www.eeoc.gov/employees-job-applicants
Vaccine Requirements
Johns Hopkins University strongly encourages, but no longer requires, at least one dose of the COVID-19 vaccine. This change does not apply to the School of Medicine (SOM). SOM hires must be fully vaccinated with an FDA COVID-19 vaccination and provide proof of vaccination status. We still require all faculty, staff, and students to receive the seasonal flu vaccine.
Exceptions to the seasonal flu vaccine or COVID-19 vaccine (for SOM) requirement(s) may be provided to individuals with sincerely held religious beliefs or medical conditions that preclude them from receiving the vaccine. Requests for an exception must be submitted to the JHU vaccination registry. For additional information, applicants for SOM positions should visit https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/coronavirus/covid-19-vaccine/ and all other JHU applicants should visit https://covidinfo.jhu.edu/health-safety/covid-vaccination-information/.
The following additional vaccine requirements may apply, depending upon your campus. Please contact the hiring department for more information.
The pre-employment physical for positions in clinical areas, laboratories, working with research subjects, or involving community contact requires documentation of immune status against Rubella (German measles), Rubeola (Measles), Mumps, Varicella (chickenpox), Hepatitis B and documentation of having received the Tdap (Tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis) vaccination. This may include documentation of having two (2) MMR vaccines; two (2) Varicella vaccines; or antibody status to these diseases from laboratory testing. Blood tests for immunities to these diseases are ordinarily included in the pre-employment physical exam except for those candidates who provide results of blood tests or immunization documentation from their own health care providers. Any vaccinations required for these diseases will be given at no cost in our Occupational Health office.

About Binghamton University:
Binghamton University is a premier public R1 research institution in the State University of New York (SUNY) system that unites more than 130 broadly interdisciplinary educational programs with some of the most vibrant research in the nation. Our unique character - shaped by our mission, outstanding academics, facilities, and community life - promotes extraordinary student success, research, and service; Binghamton University is where our students, faculty and staff thrive.
Working at Binghamton University is more than about having a great job - it is about having the opportunity to flourish in an exciting, engaging environment. Our faculty and staff appreciate Binghamton's collegial and inclusive culture and its commitment to excellence, education, innovation, and civic engagement. Our diverse campus community contributes to our success.
Binghamton merges rigorous academics, distinguished faculty who value cutting-edge, and community-engaged research, teaching and service, exceptional staff, and ultramodern facilities to engage and challenge its 18,000+ students. Our high-achieving student body represents diverse experiences from first-generation college-goers to international students. Beyond their talent, these classmates share a desire to shape the future through technology, insight, intellectual exploration, and community service.
Job Description:
ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT:
The Art History Department has developed a distinctive profile through a commitment to new theoretical perspectives and cross-disciplinary approaches to the history of art, the built environment, and the broader field of visual culture. We are committed to the mutual enrichment of teaching and research, as reflected in our distinctive undergraduate curriculum and our prominence as an innovative and markedly international center for graduate education.
ABOUT THE POSITION:
The Art History Department at Binghamton University invites applications for a tenure-track position of Assistant Professor - Asian Art, post-900 CE, beginning Fall 2027. A PhD in art history or a related field by the start date of the appointment is required. A promising record of research and experience teaching at the undergraduate and graduate level is preferred.
This position seeks to build on and reinvigorate the department's historical strength in the study of the art and culture of Asia, including Islamic art and the art and architecture of East Asia. Field and period of specialization post-900 CE are open. We especially welcome applications from those sharing our commitment to new theoretical perspectives and cross-disciplinary approaches to the discipline. The successful candidate will develop a curriculum that expands existing geographical and historical areas of concentration in the department, work collaboratively with colleagues in Art History as well as faculty in other departments and programs, and participate actively in the intellectual life of the university. The teaching and scholarship interests of the ideal candidate will include transregional and interdisciplinary approaches.
Binghamton University fosters a variety of interdisciplinary programs, including the Center for Middle East and North African Studies and the Asian and Asian American Studies Department, and our new colleague will be encouraged to contribute to one or more of these. Resources on campus to support professional and scholarly development include the School of the Arts, which fosters collaboration across its five departments (including Art History) and the Binghamton University Art Museum.
Responsibilities include teaching courses at all undergraduate and graduate levels. This position entails a 2-2 course load, with typically one undergraduate lecture and one joint undergraduate / graduate seminar offered per semester.
Requirements:
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:
PhD in art history or a related field by August 16, 2027
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Teaching experience at the undergraduate or graduate level
Published research in a peer-reviewed publication

The Department of Political Science and International Studies (POLIS) at the School of Arts and Sciences, Lebanese American University, invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant/Associate in Political Science/International Relations.
The department seeks a highly qualified and motivated candidate who is committed to excellence in innovative teaching, impactful research, and dedicated academic advising. The ideal candidate will also actively contribute to institutional development and community engagement.
Responsibilities
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in International Affairs and related areas on the Beirut and Byblos campuses.

Supervise senior study projects, MA theses, and other student research in international affairs and related fields.

Participate in departmental and university committees and other academic activities as appropriate.
Perform additional academic and administrative responsibilities as assigned by the Department in response to departmental needs and priorities.
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications
A PhD in Political Science/International Relations from a well-recognized university
Specialization in American, African, or Asian studies or a focus on International Organizations and diplomatic affairs.
Evidence of research and publication record
Evidence of teaching experience in research methods courses
Preferred Qualifications
Evidence of success in securing external funding for research
Specialization in quantitative research methods
The Department
The Department of Political and International Studies (POLIS) is dedicated to fostering the development of global leaders and citizens, advancing research to serve human progress, and upholding the values of human dignity, equity, good governance, and peace. Committed to interactive learning, interdisciplinary research, and collaborative partnerships, the department empowers students to engage with the world’s most pressing challenges while serving the broader community. It offers distinctive international cultural and educational experiences, with a strong focus on Middle East and North African studies through its BA in Political Science and International Affairs, MA in International Affairs, and Minors in Conflict Analysis and Resolution, Political Science and international affairs, and Legal Studies.
Courses are delivered in an interactive setting while being facilitated by distinguished faculty, holding PhDs from renowned American, Canadian, and European universities. Their expertise spans key areas such as Middle East and North African studies, security studies, Islamic studies, legal studies, international relations, conflict resolution, and governance. Through a dynamic blend of lectures, discussions, case studies, and experiential learning, students are encouraged to think critically and apply theoretical knowledge to real-world challenges. The department’s mission is to advance knowledge and equip students with the skills and insights necessary to lead with integrity and to serve both their communities and the global society.

Offering a unique international education experience, XJTLU brings together excellent research practice and expertise from both institutions and gives students the skills and knowledge they need to secure careers in a global marketplace. XJTLU now has over 25,000 enrolled students studying in both Suzhou and Liverpool in the UK. There are currently about 2,500 staff, including more than 1,300 academic staff from over 60 countries. XJTLU offers our undergraduates and postgraduates over 120 programmes with a diverse spectrum of courses.
With a focus on innovative education and research, XJTLU draws on the strengths of its parent universities, and plays a pivotal role in facilitating access to China for UK and other institutional partners. At the same time, XJTLU is exploring future education by blending the educational theory, best practice and culture from the West and the East.
The year 2026 marks the 20th anniversary of XJTLU. As part of its strategic priorities for the coming decade, the university is entering a new and exciting phase of development. XJTLU continues to innovate in education models, and is now transitioning from a collection of distinct approaches toward a unified, integrated Academy model a syntegrative ecosystem designed to break down silos, enhance agility, and solidify XJTLU s position at the forefront of global education and research.
For detailed information about the university, please visit www.xjtlu.edu.cn.
ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT
The Modern Languages Centre delivers high-quality language instruction and cultural education in Chinese, Japanese, and Spanish. Our team of over 50 administrative and teaching professionals employs a student-centred approach enhanced by technology and community-based learning.
RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES
There will be opportunities for Chinese language lecturer to be involved in a range of different types of delivery, such as:
Credit-bearing Chinese language modules from beginners to CEFR B2+ level, and Chinese language modules for Specific Purposes, i.e. Business Chinese.
Credit-bearing Chinese content modules for degree students majoring in Teaching Chinese as an International Language and China Studies, i.e. Modern Chinese or Classical Chinese.
Non-credit bearing Chinese courses, i.e. Practical Chinese Courses and Summer School.
Engaging with Continuing Support Chinese language and cultural activities.
Mentoring students on their internship and FYP projects.
HSK item design and invigilation.
There will also be the opportunity for Chinese language lecturer to take on a managerial role with responsibility for the coordination and leadership of the Chinese teaching programmes.
Additionally, there are opportunities for all staff to develop their careers by taking on wider managerial and administrative roles, as well as by contributing to both hub and university-level committees.
All managerial, administrative and committee roles are appointed to on a fixed-term basis, thus providing all staff members with a range of options to take on responsibilities in areas that interest them.
ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCE:
Successful applicants should be educated to Master s degree level in a relevant discipline (e.g. Teaching Chinese as an International Language or Chinese Language and Literature), and should have at least two years of post-master s relevant teaching experience, preferably at university level. Additionally, applicants should have a good standard of written and spoken English, as this is the working language of the university. Familiarity with more than one language proficiency standard such as CEFR/HSK/ACTFL is a plus.
We are particularly interested in receiving applications from candidates who can demonstrate a dynamic, current and innovative engagement in one or more of the following areas: technology-enhanced language learning and assessment design; culture and language integrated learning; Chinese for specific purposes; communicative and task-based methodologies and project-based language learning.
CAREER DEVELOPMENT
Clear career development path with annual review.
Professional development trainings are provided.
COMPENSATION & BENEFITS
SALARY: Competitive salary in the market
BENEFITS
Allowance: XJTLU provide various month/annual/one-off allowances as
Housing allowance
Travel allowance
Relocation allowance
Etc.

Paid holidays:
Statutory Holidays (13 days)
Full Paid Holidays (34 days per academic year including university close days and annual leave)
Family Matters Leave
Paid Sick Leave
Marriage Leave
Paternity Leave
Parental Leave
Etc.
HOW TO APPLY
Please submit your application on our university website by Click https://career15.sapsf.cn/sfcareer/jobreqcareer?jobId=4468&company=xjtlu
Applications must be submitted in a single pdf file that includes 3 parts in the order of:
A cover letter that explains how you fulfil the criteria specified in this job description
A current CV (both Chinese and English preferred), specifying for each work experience whether it was full-time or part-time and including education background with years of study.
Contact Details for Three References
For enquiries relating to the position, please email to HR at Jia.Xu@xjtlu.edu.cn. Please quote the position and Position ID 4468 in your enquiry.

Job Details
Assistant/Associate Teaching Professor, Accounting
Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Cornell University
The Cornell SC Johnson College of Business invites applicants for an Assistant Teaching Professor (3-year renewable term) or Associate Teaching Professor (5-year renewable term) position in the Accounting area, with a school affiliation in the Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management. Candidates would be appointed at the rank that is appropriate given their experience and performance. The intended start date of this position is July 1, 2027. The position will be based in Ithaca, NY, with teaching responsibilities completed in person on the Ithaca campus in both fall and spring semesters.
This is an academic-year (i.e., 9 month) appointment. Responsibilities of the position include teaching five three-credit courses per year in financial accounting, managerial accounting, tax, auditing, and/or related accounting courses to undergraduate and graduate students. Preference will be given to applicants who can teach multiple topics. Teaching assignments may change to meet the needs of the curriculum, as determined by College leadership. Although the primary role for this position is teaching, the School expects faculty to participate in student and school events including student advising, school projects, etc. The successful applicant will also be expected to maintain current AACSB standards for a scholarly academic (SA) or scholarly practitioner (SP), depending on their qualifications.
The ideal candidate will possess a PhD in accounting or closely related field. Candidates holding a Masters' degree in accounting also will be considered, and preference will be given to such candidates with professional experience in accounting and certification as a CPA, CMA, CIA, and/or equivalent. Candidates should have extensive experience effectively teaching accounting at the undergraduate, MBA, and/or executive MBA levels, as demonstrated through course evaluations, and have a sincere enthusiasm for teaching, student support, and collegial interaction.
The Cornell SC Johnson College of Business includes three Schools: the Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management (Johnson), the Charles H. Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management (Dyson), and the Nolan School of Hotel Administration (Nolan). It is expected that our faculty teach across multiple schools within the College of Business.
To be considered for this position, apply at https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/32757. For full consideration please ensure that your application is complete by November 15, 2026. Review of applications will begin immediately after that date and continue until the position has been filled. Applications received after November 15, 2026 will be reviewed if the position has not been filled.
The following materials are required:
1. Letter of interest, with clear indication of position being applied for;
2. Curriculum vitae;
3. Three recommendation letters;
4. Report of courses taught and evidence of teaching effectiveness; and
5. Any other supporting documents, such as curriculum development materials or research papers (if applicable).
Consistent with Cornell's practice, appointment to academic positions requires candidates to disclose relevant information about their prior employment including whether they have been found to have violated institutional or employer policies related to or governing unlawful discrimination and harassment, academic and research misconduct, or financial misconduct.
In compliance with New York's Pay Transparency Act, the minimum annual base salary range for this position is $105,000 - $200,000. This pay range represents base pay only (for 9 months, paid over 12 months) and excludes any additional items such as incentives, bonuses, additional pay for overload teaching, or other items. Cornell University considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and organizational considerations when extending an offer.

Tampa

Position Details
POSITION SUMMARY
The Department of History, Geography, and Legal Studies in the College of Social Sciences, Mathematics and Education at the University of Tampa invites applications for a tenure-track position in United States and the World History Since 1945 at the rank of Assistant Professor starting in August 2027. The Department welcomes candidates from all specializations within this field, but applications from candidates whose teaching and research includes civil rights, human rights, or social movements are especially desirable.
The successful candidate will be responsible for teaching three, 4-credit courses per semester, or six per year. Applicants are expected to demonstrate a commitment to excellence in teaching and to engaging students in learning beyond the classroom. Successful candidates must have at least two years of full-time, in-person teaching experience at the post-secondary level.
Applicants will have demonstrated scholarship in their area of expertise. Other responsibilities include student advising, and service to the department, college and University.
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience.
QUALIFICATIONS
The successful candidate must have a Ph.D. in History. (ABD will not be considered.) Applicants must show evidence of outstanding teaching and demonstrate the ability to teach a wide variety of courses that engage History majors as well as general education students. Finally, the candidate must show evidence of an active research agenda, with the potential to involve undergraduate majors in their work.

All required documents listed below should be uploaded to the attachment box at the bottom of the "My Experience" page of the application before continuing through the application.
• Cover letter
• Curriculum vitae
• 250-word statement describing how you have successfully engaged students in your classes
• 500-word statement of research agenda
• Recent course evaluations
• Graduate transcript (unofficial is acceptable for initial review)
• Contact information for at least four professional references
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.

The University of Tampa is a medium-sized, comprehensive, residentially based private institution of more than 11,000 undergraduate and graduate students. The University is ideally situated on a beautiful 110-acre campus next to the Hillsborough River, adjacent to Tampa's dynamic central business district, which is a growing, vibrant, diverse metropolitan area. Graduate programs include a M.S. in Criminology and Criminal Justice, a M.Ed. in Curriculum & Instruction, a M.Ed. in Educational Leadership, and a M.S. in Instructional Design and Technology. Our faculty are excellent teachers and scholars who engage their students both in and out of the classroom. Our college continually fosters relationships with governmental, not-for-profit, and community organizations in the greater Tampa Bay region to provide students with the opportunity to pursue an internship, volunteer, or interact with professionals working in their chosen field. Each department also offers study abroad courses that students can take for credit toward their degree. For more information, see https://www.ut.edu/academics/college-of-social-sciences-mathematics-and-education.
The faculty and administrators in CSSME, along with professional staff across the University, will provide meaningful support for your teaching and scholarship as elements of your personal and career development. The vision of the College of Social Sciences, Mathematics, and Education is "Empowering learners to make a difference." All candidates are expected to contribute to the diversity of our curriculum and community. We are searching for teacher-scholars who will serve as mentors for our diverse student body, and who have a demonstrated commitment to the academic success of all students.
The University of Tampa is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to excellence through diversity and does not discriminate based on age, race, sex, disability, sexual orientation, national origin, religion, marital status, gender identity, veteran status, or any other non-job-related criteria. The University of Tampa recognizes the importance of a multicultural community of students, faculty, and staff who seek to advance our commitment to diversity. Submission Guidelines
To receive full consideration for a faculty appointment with The University of Tampa, please be sure to upload documents as required for this position at time of application submission. Once your application has been submitted, no changes may be made. Description
The San Diego State University Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry seeks to hire a tenure-track assistant professor with expertise in AI-enabled Chemical Discovery, broadly defined. We seek candidates employing cutting-edge interdisciplinary approaches developing artificial intelligence applications for chemical questions. Relevant AI-enabling research areas may include, but are not limited to, reaction discovery and optimization, synthesis planning, catalyst and reagent design, mechanistic analysis, and prediction or control of chemical reactivity and selectivity; molecular and biomolecular structure, function, and design, including generative design of biological systems; chemical biology; and the discovery of functional molecules and materials. Approaches integrating AI with experimental chemistry, automated or closed-loop experimentation, chemical theory, or simulation are encouraged. Applicants from anywhere within the chemical science continuum are invited, as long as the development of AI-enabled approaches is a central focus. Apply via PageUp by October 22, 2026.
The Department of Chemistry/Biochemistry is home to dynamic faculty, state-of-the-art facilities, a competitive Joint Doctoral Program and numerous cross-disciplinary Master's programs. Faculty benefit from robust institutional support, including access to core facilities and partnerships with external organizations. SDSU is part of a strong research ecosystem in San Diego encompassing a thriving biotechnology sector, multiple academic research institutions (Salk Institute, Scripps Research, University of California San Diego) and multiple academic clinical centers (Moores Cancer Center, Rady Children's Hospital). SDSU champions the teacher-scholar model of academic research where faculty effort is equally split between teaching and mentoring students, and research. To learn more, please visit https://chemistry.sdsu.edu/.
Qualifications
Required qualifications by date of application
A strong record of original research achievements, along with demonstrated ability to: (a) establish and sustain a vigorous, independent, and externally funded research program; (b) effectively teach both undergraduate and graduate courses; and (c) actively contribute to service activities within the university and the broader professional community.
Demonstration of past accomplishments and/or future plans in at least three (3) of the “Building on Inclusive Excellence” criteria (https://fs-diversity.sdsu.edu/recruitment/guidance-candidates).
Required qualifications by date of hire:
Terminal degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Computer Science or a closely related field, with all degree requirements met.
Preferred qualifications:
Postdoctoral or equivalent research experience.
Demonstrated expertise in developing or substantively integrating artificial intelligence, machine-learning, or data-driven methods to address chemical or biochemical questions.
A research program that combines methodological innovation with chemically or biochemically meaningful discovery and validation.
Potential to build interdisciplinary collaborations across experimental, computational, and theoretical research areas.
Evidence of effective teaching or mentoring in chemistry, biochemistry, computation, data science, or related disciplines.
Application Instructions
Apply via PageUp by October 22, 2026, providing the following materials:
Cover letter, indicating how the applicant meets or will meet required qualifications, preferred qualifications, and “Building on Inclusive Excellence” criteria (maximum 1 page)
Curriculum vita including names and contact information for three references

Copies of up to 3 relevant publications

jobs.description:
Job Details
Faculty Personnel and Instructional Support Coordinator (Administrative Support Coordinator II)
Job No: 562322
Work Type: Staff
Locations: Southern California: San Diego
Categories: Bargaining Unit: Unit 7 - CSUEU - Clerical and Administrative Support Services, Job Search Category/Discipline: Administrative, Appointment Type: Temporary, Time Basis: Full Time, Workplace Type (Exclude Inst Fac): Telecommute eligible (work onsite as scheduled and/or as requested and telecommute as scheduled)
Position Summary
Are you a highly organized administrative professional who thrives on managing complex processes, deadlines, and details? The College of Arts and Letters is seeking a Faculty Personnel and Instructional Support Coordinator to support critical faculty personnel and academic administration processes across the College. This position plays an important role in ensuring faculty evaluations, advancement processes, workload reporting, and other instructional activities are coordinated accurately, consistently, and on time.
Working closely with the Director of Resource Management, Instructional Analyst, Administrative Analyst, faculty, department staff, college leadership, and campus partners, the Coordinator serves as a central resource for navigating established faculty personnel processes and requirements. This role is ideal for someone who excels at managing confidential information, maintaining detailed records, coordinating multiple high-stakes timelines, and providing clear procedural guidance in a complex academic environment.
Key Responsibilities
Faculty Evaluation & Advancement: Coordinate college-wide faculty review processes, including reappointment, tenure and promotion (RTP), cumulative and periodic evaluations, and lecturer range elevation, ensuring required documentation and deadlines are completed accurately.
Process & Records Coordination: Initiate and monitor faculty personnel cases, review materials for completeness and procedural compliance, maintain confidential records, and coordinate corrections or follow-up with faculty, departments, committees, and campus partners.
Faculty Workload Administration: Coordinate faculty workload and assigned-time processes, review departmental submissions for completeness and consistency, maintain records, and track required documentation, evaluations, and deadlines.
Reporting & Reconciliation: Compile workload and assigned-time reports, maintain supporting spreadsheets and documentation, and coordinate with the Instructional Analyst to identify and resolve discrepancies across workload, appointment, and instructional resource information.
Faculty & Department Support: Serve as a resource to faculty and department administrative staff by communicating requirements, providing procedural guidance and training, and supporting navigation of established faculty personnel and workload processes.
Operational Continuity: Provide administrative coverage to departments, programs, centers, and institutes during vacancies, staff transitions, peak processing periods, or other periods requiring additional faculty and academic administrative support.
Why Join Us?
Support Faculty Success: Play an important role in the processes that support faculty advancement, evaluation, appointments, and academic work across the College.
Develop Specialized Expertise: Build in-depth knowledge of faculty personnel administration, RTP, workload, assigned time, and higher education academic operations.
Work Across the College: Collaborate with faculty, department staff, college leadership, and university partners across a large and diverse academic organization.
Take Ownership of Complex Processes: Manage detailed, deadline-driven work where accuracy, organization, confidentiality, and follow-through are essential.
Make a College-Wide Impact: Help ensure critical faculty and instructional processes operate consistently and effectively across the College of Arts and Letters.
Position Information
This is a full-time (1.0 time-base), benefits-eligible, temporary position. The anticipated end date will be one year from the start date, with the possibility of reappointment.
This position is designated non-exempt under FLSA and is eligible for overtime compensation.
Standard SDSU work hours are Monday – Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but may vary based on operational needs.
This position is approved for one day of telecommuting after an initial training period with onsite work in San Diego.
As part of the California State University (CSU) system, San Diego State University helps power one of the largest and most impactful public university systems in the nation. See what it's like to work at the CSU—watch our video and imagine your future here: Working at the CSU.
Department Summary
The College of Arts and Letters (CAL) is dedicated to advancing the study of human expression, culture, language, history, governance, and creative practice. Through innovative teaching, research, and community engagement, the College prepares students to think critically, communicate effectively, and engage responsibly in a complex global society. CAL supports a wide range of academic departments, interdisciplinary programs, centers, and initiatives that foster intellectual inquiry, cultural understanding, civic engagement, and ethical leadership. The College is committed to inclusive excellence, academic rigor, and collaborative partnerships that connect scholarship to public life.
For more information regarding the College of Arts and Letters, click here.
Education and Experience
Entry to this classification requires a fully functional knowledge of and skill in standard office procedures and practices, as well as an ability to understand and operate in a variety of organizational structures. Additionally, incumbents are expected to have a thorough knowledge of English grammar, spelling, and punctuation and be able to clearly communicate orally and in writing. Some positions may require a knowledge of business mathematics beyond basic arithmetic. The ability to use and quickly learn new office support technology systems and software packages is also a prerequisite.
These qualifications would normally be obtained through a high school program, technical/vocational program, or their equivalents combined with several years of related office work experience.
Key Qualifications
Extensive experience using Microsoft Word and Excel.
Experience with OnBase, Banner, and PeopleSoft.
Experience in handling confidential matters
Experience coordinating administrative support functions for a group.
Compensation and Benefits
San Diego State University offers competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being and professional growth.

Step placement will be determined based on relevant qualifications and professional experience, in alignment with the department's budget and equity guidelines.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Purpose of Position
The Department of Psychological Science at Northern Kentucky University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Psychology beginning August 2027. Candidates should be strongly committed to teaching at the undergraduate level, engaging undergraduates in research, and applying rigorous scientific principles to the study of psychology. Area of specialization is open. Preference will be given to candidates with expertise in clinical/counseling psychology, lifespan development, industrial/organizational psychology, or human factors. The department offers a collegial work environment that values both teaching and scholarship. Departmental scholarly interests span clinical, developmental, health, social, cognitive, and industrial/organizational psychology, along with neuroscience and psychopharmacology. More information about the department can be found on our website https://www.nku.edu/academics/artsci/about/departments/psychology/about.html.
Northern Kentucky University (NKU) is a public, comprehensive university of approximately 15,000 students supported by more than 2,000 faculty and staff. Located on a vibrant suburban campus in Highland Heights—just seven miles southeast of downtown Cincinnati—we deliver innovative, learner‑centered education and conduct impactful scholarship that prepares students for rewarding careers while strengthening the region’s social and economic vitality.
NKU’s vision is that we will be nationally recognized for being a student-ready, regionally engaged university that empowers diverse learners for economic and social mobility. Our core values place emphasis on our culture of excellence, creativity, innovation, and collegiality.
Our strategic framework emphasizes (1) expanding and enhancing student access, success, and career readiness, (2) creating a supportive and sustainable work environment to attract and retain talent, and (3) advancing economic, social, and civic vitality in our community and region. The University provides equal opportunities in educational services and employment according to the law.
Primary Responsibilities
The successful candidate will teach undergraduate in-person classes, as well as courses offered for our online BA program. In-person and online courses will include Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods and Lab, and courses aligned with the candidate’s expertise.
The successful candidate will also maintain an active, peer-reviewed research agenda consistent with the department’s emphasis on scientific rigor.
Qualifications
A Ph.D. in psychology from a regionally or nationally accredited university by August 1, 2027, is required.
Candidates should submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, teaching statement, research statement including a plan for incorporating undergraduate students, up to three reprints/preprints, and names and email addresses of three references. Candidates with teaching experience should also submit evidence of teaching proficiency (e.g., teaching evaluations, example syllabi, etc.). The cover letter and teaching statement should show, as a faculty member at NKU, how the candidate will contribute to our core values and our strategic framework, especially in how the candidate will contribute to student success and belonging.
Application materials should be submitted electronically to https://jobs.nku.edu/. Once an application has been processed, a secure link will be sent to the three reference providers so that letters of recommendation can be uploaded to the same website.
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.
Questions about the position can be directed to the chair of the search committee, Dr. Kim Breitenbecher (breitenbeche@nku.edu, 859-572-5519).

The School Psychology program, within the Department of Education and Human Services, at Lehigh University invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor with a specialization in intervention research with neurodiverse populations. The individual hired will be expected to teach coursework that aligns with the APA and NASP accredited School Psychology program curriculum including topics related to: health/pediatric school psychology, school-wide programs to address health care needs of students, child psychopathology, and/or advanced school and family interventions, at the graduate level. There will also be opportunities for the faculty member to teach classes in the Board Certified Behavior Analysis program within the broader College of Education (if they hold the BCBA credential). Georgia College & State University (GCSU) is the state's designated public liberal arts university, where students learn the essential skills to compete in a fast-paced and technology-driven global society. The university prepares students for successful careers, leadership in communities, problem solving and life-long learning through personalized attention in a residential setting with opportunities for a variety of transformational experiences through its award-winning, high-impact practices. One of only three selective universities within the University System of Georgia and a top 10 ranked public university in the Southeast, GCSU offers undergraduate degrees in more than 40 majors, more than 30 graduate programs, doctorates in education and nursing, professional certificates, and continuing education programs.
As a member of the prestigious Council of Public Liberal Arts Colleges (COPLAC), GCSU is committed to fostering a liberal arts environment that values academic preeminence, interdisciplinary inquiry and an inclusive learning community. GCSU enjoys a strong reputation for academic excellence and nationally ranked programs according to US News & World Report, The Princeton Review and Colleges of Distinction - among other ranking sources.
Georgia College & State University takes great pride in combining the educational experience of a private liberal arts college with the affordability of a public university. Faculty and staff are dedicated to student engagement and experiential learning through high-impact practices such as internships, service- and community-based learning, leadership development, study abroad opportunities, mentored undergraduate research and a capstone project that fosters intellectual curiosity, reasoned inquiry and critical thinking.
The university's beautiful and historic campus is located downtown in Milledgeville, Georgia, a charming, diverse college town of approximately 19,000 residents in Central Georgia, and only 90 miles southeast of Atlanta. Milledgeville is also the home of noted American author and alumna, Flannery O'Connor, '45, and the college community enjoys many exciting literary arts programs at O'Connor's former home, Andalusia, a National Historic Landmark owned by the university. Milledgeville is located on the banks of beautiful Lake Sinclair and Lake Oconee, allowing faculty, staff and students to take full advantage of the environmental and recreational benefits of being part of a lake community. Our 29 full-time faculty members support approximately 395 undergraduate Biology majors, 112 Environmental Science majors, and 26 graduate students. jobs.title: Assistant Professor Position in Analytical Chemistry
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Department of Chemistry at Colby College invites applications for a tenure-track, Assistant Professor position in analytical chemistry to begin fall 2027. We welcome applications from analytical chemists in all disciplines with preference for expertise in environmental applications, particularly in aqueous or terrestrial settings. Candidates must have earned a Ph.D. in chemistry or a related field by the position start date, demonstrate a commitment to teaching undergraduate General Chemistry and Analytical chemistry, and be able to contribute to our environmental chemistry curriculum. Qualified candidates will also demonstrate a strong commitment to building an active research program involving undergraduate students. The Colby Chemistry Department offers excellent instrumentation and computational resources to support analytical work. The College has a vibrant program in environmental sciences bridging multiple departments and partnerships with regional institutions such as Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences, The Seven Lakes Alliance, and Colby’s Island Campus. For more information about this position, please see: https://web.colby.edu/analytical/. Interested candidates should submit a letter of application that describes their interests and qualifications for the position. Applicants must also submit a current curriculum vitae, a statement of research interests, a statement of teaching philosophy, undergraduate and graduate transcripts, three confidential letters of recommendation, and two samples of current scholarship (e.g., a recent publication or manuscript) as PDFs to: https://apply.interfolio.com/194052. Colby is committed to fostering a diverse community of scholars, and application materials should address supporting Colby’s commitment to inclusive teaching. The position carries an average annual teaching load of 4.5 courses. The anticipated salary range for this position is $92,700 to $96,700, commensurate with rank, experience, qualifications, and other relevant factors. Research is supported with a competitive startup package. Application review will begin October 9, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. Inquiries may be directed to analytical@colby.edu.
Colby is a private, coeducational liberal arts college that admits students and makes personnel decisions on the basis of the individual’s qualifications to contribute to Colby’s educational objectives and institutional needs. The principle of not discriminating on the basis of race, color, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, caste, national or ethnic origin, marital status, genetic information, political beliefs, veteran or military status, parental status, pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions, or physical or mental disability unrelated to the job or course of study requirements is consistent with the mission of a liberal arts college and the law.

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor of Nuclear Engineering, Fall 2027
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Department of Nuclear Engineering at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (UTK) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor level. The department will pursue tenure consideration for qualified candidates. The anticipated start date is August 2027.
Duties include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in nuclear engineering-related subjects, developing and sustaining an externally funded research program, advising graduate students, publishing scholarly work, and providing service to the department, college, university, and professional community.
The UT Department of Nuclear Engineering is the largest Nuclear Engineering PhD program in the United States, with a diverse research portfolio and close collaborations with Idaho National Laboratory (INL), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), the Y-12 National Security Complex, and more than 150 nuclear-related companies within 50 miles of the campus. The department is housed in the state-of-the-art Zeanah Engineering Complex, home to more than 20 nuclear engineering laboratories and computational resources. The department is committed to cultivating work/life balance and a family-friendly environment for faculty, staff, and students.
The Tickle College of Engineering (TCE), comprised of nine departments that house 213 tenure-track and BO+ non-tenure-track faculty, is in the midst of unprecedented growth under Chancellor Donde Plowman and Dean Matthew Mench, having added 30+ new faculty over the past 4 years and set records in research expenditures ($113.9M in FY25J, enrollment (4,800 undergraduate and 1,500 graduate students), and increased ranking (now 28th among public universities) in the US News and World Report list of top engineering colleges. Key partnerships with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Consolidated Nuclear Security (Y-12) and growth are supported by new facilities including the Zeanah Engineering Complex and the Innovation South building.
Knoxville is a vibrant city with a beautiful, walkable downtown, active neighborhoods, a lively nightlife with numerous theaters and museums, a rich live music scene, and eclectic dining. Nestled in the foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains and surrounded by lakes and the Tennessee River, Knoxville offers outstanding access to outdoor recreation and is within 200 miles of four major metropolitan areas.
Qualifications
We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests strengthen and broaden the department's capabilities in one or more of the following areas: reliability and maintainability of nuclear systems and components; data analytics, artificial intelligence, digital twin technologies, and cyber security for nuclear applications; nuclear instrumentation and control; radiation instrumentation; robust decision-making, empirical/data-driven modeling, and process & equipment monitoring; thermal-fluid sciences and experimental reactor thermal-hydraulics. Candidates whose work bridges experimentation, computational modeling, sensing, and thermal­fluid or reactor systems analysis in support of reliable, sustainable nuclear power are especially encouraged to apply. Ideally, successful candidates will be able to contribute across more than one of these areas. Preference will be given to applicants with demonstrated (or clearly emerging, for more junior candidates) research success that complements existing departmental strengths and who have a vision for developing collaborative, sustainably funded research programs. Candidates must also show strong commitment to high-quality undergraduate and graduate teaching.
Candidates for assistant professor must have a demonstrated potential to develop a nationally recognized, externally funded research program. Candidates for associate professor must lead a nationally recognized externally funded research program and demonstrate the potential to develop an international recognized research program.
Applicants must hold a doctorate in Nuclear Engineering or a closely related field by the effective date of appointment.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant Professor - Bengali History and Culture
Date Posted: 09/17/2026
Closing Date: 10/26/2026, 11:59PM ET
Req ID: 49201
Job Category: Faculty - Tenure Stream (continuing)
Faculty/Division: University of Toronto Mississauga

Campus: University of Toronto Mississauga (UTM)
Existing Vacancy: Yes
POSITION DESCRIPTION
The Department of Historical Studies at the University of Toronto Mississauga invites applications for a full-time tenure stream position in Bengali History and Culture. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.
The successful candidate will teach undergraduate courses in History and South Asian Studies on the Mississauga campus (UTM) and will hold a graduate appointment in the Department for the Study of Religion on the St. George campus.
This search aligns with the University’s commitment to strategically and proactively promote diversity among our community members (Statement on Equity, Diversity & Excellence). Recognizing that Black, Indigenous, and other Racialized communities have experienced inequities that have developed historically and are ongoing, we strongly welcome and encourage candidates from those communities to apply.
REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS
Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in South Asia area studies or a related area by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching in the history and religions of Bengal. The successful candidate must demonstrate linguistic mastery in Bengali and training and proficiency in other South Asian languages. The geographic scope of their work must cut across what are today the national boundaries of India and Bangladesh, with a focus on language, nationalism, and/or environmental history. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and enhance our existing departmental strengths.
Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence which can be demonstrated through a record of publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals or forthcoming publications that meet high international standards; the submitted research statement; presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; and strong endorsements from referees.
Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier (including the required materials outlined below, as well as evidence of superior performance in other teaching-related activities), and strong letters of reference. Other teaching-related activities can include performance as a teaching assistant or course instructor, experience leading successful workshops or seminars, student mentorship, or excellent conference presentations or posters.
RESPONSIBILITIES
The successful candidate will be expected to pursue innovative and independent research, and to establish an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program.
In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load.
The successful candidate will teach in the History and South Asian Humanities programs housed in the Department of Historical Studies at UTM. They will be able to offer a broad range of courses from the introductory to the advanced undergraduate level. At the graduate level, the successful candidate will have opportunities for teaching, supervision, and mentorship in the Department for the Study of Religion housed on the University of Toronto’s St. George campus
HIRING SALARY RANGE
The expected salary range is $135,000 - $160,000 CAD per annum, depending on experience. Negotiations beyond this salary range will be considered for exceptionally qualified candidates.
ABOUT US
The transdisciplinary Department of Historical Studies at the University of Toronto Mississauga encompasses programs in Classical Civilization, Diaspora and Transnational Studies, History, History of Religions, and Women, Gender and Sexuality Studies. For more information about our department, please visit our home page.
For more information on working at the University of Toronto, please visit https://www.utoronto.ca/research-innovation/working-at-uoft.
At UTM we are committed to fostering an environment of diversity and inclusion. With an enviably diverse student body, we especially welcome applications from candidates who identify as Indigenous, Black, or racially visible (persons of colour), and who have experience working with, teaching or mentoring diverse groups or students. Candidates must demonstrate, in their application materials, an ability to foster diversity on campus and within the curriculum or discipline, and must show evidence of a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and the promotion of a respectful and collegial environment. Candidates must submit a statement describing their contributions to equity, diversity, and inclusion, which might cover topics such as (but not limited to): teaching that incorporates a focus on underrepresented communities; efforts undertaken to develop inclusive pedagogies, collaboration, and engagement with underrepresented communities; and mentoring of students from underrepresented groups. If you have questions about this statement, please contact Dr. Brian Gettler, Acting Chair, Department of Historical Studies at hs.chair@utoronto.ca.
APPLICATION PROCESS
All application materials, including recent reference letters, must be received by October 26, 2026.
All qualified candidates are invited to apply online by clicking the link below. Your CV and cover letter should be uploaded into the dedicated fields. Please combine additional application materials into one or two files in PDF/MS Word format. Applicants must submit the following materials:
a cover letter;
a current curriculum vitae;
a research statement outlining current and future research interests;
a recent writing sample;
an equity, diversity, and inclusion statement (as noted above);
a teaching dossier, including
a teaching statement,
sample course materials, and
teaching evaluations or evidence of superior performance in other teaching-related activities as listed above; and
the name and contact information of three references.
The University of Toronto’s recruiting tool will automatically solicit and collect letters of reference from each referee within 48 hours of an application being submitted. Applicants remain responsible for ensuring that referees submit recent letters (on letterhead, dated and signed) by the closing date. Submission guidelines and details on the automatic reference letter collection, including timelines, are available in the candidate FAQ.
If you have any questions about this position, please contact Dr. Brian Gettler, Acting Chair, Department of Historical Studies at hs.chair@utoronto.ca.
